docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
scanpath-studio launches the app. Use these commands to create figures, check data and manage saved work without opening the app:

Command What it does scanpath-studio, run Launch the app render Write one trial's scanpath, heatmap or replay to a file publication Export a saved figure recipe or open it as an offline editor corpus Render a corpus figure from a tidy CSV you already have recipe Recreate a cohort profile CSV from its saved recipe check Run the Data checks on your tables add Add your tables to the app's dataset list remove Remove a dataset you added from that list annotations Read or write a dataset's favorites, tags and notes open Open the app on a dataset you added, at a reading and figure cache Show or clear the recovery cache version Show the build, and whether a newer release is out cite Print how to cite Scanpath Studio

Each command takes --help, and scanpath-studio --version prints the version. If you mistype a command, the CLI suggests the closest match.

docs.title: Publication
docs.text:
Download the editable file under Save or open to reproduce the figure with its crop, labels, caption and print settings.

scanpath-studio render --sample --screen Paragraph --width-mm 85 -o reading.publication.json
scanpath-studio publication reading.publication.json -o reading.html
scanpath-studio publication figure-2.json -o figure-2.pdf

Choose SVG, PDF, PNG or TIFF for artwork, or MP4 for a selected replay clip. Rendering these files requires a Chromium browser. The HTML editor is self-contained and can be used offline.

docs.title: Launch the app
docs.text:
scanpath-studio
scanpath-studio --server.port 8600
scanpath-studio --no-persist          # don't cache the session on this computer
scanpath-studio --download-dir D:\corpora  # where ⬇ Download saves public datasets

scanpath-studio run … is the same. Any other launch flag is passed on to streamlit run.

The app listens on this computer only (127.0.0.1), and it has no login. To serve it to other machines on a network you trust, pass --server.address 0.0.0.0, or set server.address in a Streamlit config.toml or STREAMLIT_SERVER_ADDRESS:

scanpath-studio --server.address 0.0.0.0

Served on a network, the app turns off the controls that read or write the server's folders, because any visitor could use them. These are the Data directory box, the folder picker, and ⬇ Download for the public datasets and stimulus-image folders. On a lab server you trust, turn them back on with SCANPATH_LOCAL_FS=1 (SCANPATH_LOCAL_FS=1 scanpath-studio --server.address 0.0.0.0).

docs.title: render
docs.text:
render writes one trial to a file without opening the app. The file extension sets the format: .html opens as an interactive figure in your browser, while .png, .svg and .pdf need Chrome, Chromium or Edge (or run plotly_get_chrome -y once; see the FAQ). The figure is the app's Scanpath design unless a flag changes it, and every figure option has a flag.

# List the trials to pick from
scanpath-studio render --sample --list-trials

# The bundled demo: each reading has several screens, so name the one to draw
scanpath-studio render --sample --screen Paragraph -o scanpath.html

# Your own data (replace p1 / t3 with IDs from --list-trials)
scanpath-studio render \
  --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv \
  --participant p1 --trial t3 --output scanpath.svg

# A draft file saved from the app's Draw a scanpath screen
scanpath-studio render --authoring authored-scanpath.json -o authored.html

# A public dataset, loaded as the app loads it (downloaded on first use)
scanpath-studio render --potec ./potec --list-trials
scanpath-studio render --onestop ./onestop --onestop-variant public \
  --onestop-regime ordinary --onestop-part Paragraph --list-trials

The Python API loads the same datasets with load_potec and load_onestop.

docs.title: Common tasks
docs.text:
Goal Flags add a layer --word-boxes, --fixation-index, --heatmap hide a layer --no-text, --no-fixations, --no-saccades animate --animate, optionally --playback-speed X. The replay uses every styling flag it can draw and names the rest in a warning set the screen size --canvas WIDTHxHEIGHT. --crop-to-data frames the data instead of the whole screen, with --crop-margin PX around it (default: 5% of the data's extent, at least 20 px) color fixations --color-by FIELD, including a column of your own once --keep-columns COLUMN… carries it through loading size fixations by duration --marker-size-scale sqrt\|linear\|log\|relative (default sqrt), --marker-duration-range LO HI (ms, default 50 600), --marker-size-range MIN MAX (px), --duration-size-legend (show the optional size key) draw only part of a trial --fix-index-range START:END (1-based, both inclusive; --animate and --compare-with honor it too) draw the stimulus --stimulus-image PATH for one image. --show-stimulus-image draws each trial's stimulus image, named in the image_path column (--sample ships its images). --image-root DIR --image-pattern '{text_id}.png' fills image_path from a folder smooth the heatmap --heatmap-style smoothed --heatmap-sigma 20 (σ in px; leave it out for an automatic σ) style the word boxes --word-box-color, --word-box-line-opacity, --word-box-fill-color, --word-box-fill-opacity. A fill opacity of 0 draws outlines only, and a line opacity of 0 the fill only size the figure --width, --height, --scale. For print, --width-mm MM or --width-in IN with --dpi N (default 300) add a title and caption --title, --caption write each layer to its own file --separable-layers print the equivalent code --print-code python (or cli / both), plus --print-code-explicit

Hover fields appear in the order you list them. For a column named pupil, left, preserve the comma with --keep-columns 'pupil, left' --fixation-hover-fields-json '["duration_ms","pupil, left"]'. Use --fixation-hover-fields-json '[]' to clear that selection. The Words layer accepts --word-hover-fields-json in the same way.

docs.title: Compare two scanpaths
docs.text:
--compare-participant ID --compare-trial ID selects the second reading, B. For example, --compare-participant B --compare-trial 'round:2' preserves the colon in the trial ID. The shorthand --compare-with PARTICIPANT:TRIAL splits at the last colon.

# Two participants on the same paragraph, overlaid
scanpath-studio render --sample -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph \
  --compare-with l7_183:l7_183_2_1_1_Ele --compare-screen Paragraph -o compare.html

# The same overlay, drawing only B's word boxes and text
scanpath-studio render --sample -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph \
  --compare-with l7_183:l7_183_2_1_1_Ele --compare-screen Paragraph --compare-stimulus b \
  -o compare_b.html

# Side by side: each panel draws its trial's stimulus
scanpath-studio render --sample -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph \
  --compare-with l7_183:l7_183_2_1_1_Ele --compare-screen Paragraph \
  --compare-layout side-by-side -o compare.svg

# A style for each scanpath
scanpath-studio render --sample -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph \
  --compare-with l7_183:l7_183_2_1_1_Ele --compare-screen Paragraph \
  --style-a fix_color=#D55E00,opacity=0.5 --style-b saccade_style=dash \
  -o compare_styled.html

# B from a second dataset
scanpath-studio render --words ia.csv --fixations fix.csv -p p1 -t t1 \
  --compare-with p1:t1 \
  --compare-words other/ia.csv --compare-fixations other/fix.csv \
  --compare-dataset-name "Our lab" \
  --canvas 1680x1050 --compare-canvas 1680x1050 \
  -o cross.html
Goal Flags pick B --compare-participant ID --compare-trial ID pick each screen of a multipart trial --screen ID (A), --compare-screen ID (B); each defaults to its trial's first screen arrange the panels --compare-layout {overlay,side-by-side,stacked} (default overlay) choose whose stimulus an overlay draws --compare-stimulus {both,a,b} (default both) name the two scanpaths --label-a TEXT --label-b TEXT (both or neither) style each scanpath --style-a SPEC, --style-b SPEC (keys below) leave out the A/B legend --no-compare-legend give B a separate stimulus image (side by side or stacked) --stimulus-image-b PATH, with --stimulus-image-size-b WxH / --stimulus-image-origin-b X,Y take B from another dataset --compare-words PATH… --compare-fixations PATH…, plus --compare-raw-gaze PATH… and --compare-dataset-name NAME map B's columns yourself --compare-word-schema JSON, --compare-fix-schema JSON, --compare-raw-gaze-schema JSON, as --word-schema and its siblings map A's set the two screen sizes --canvas WxH, --compare-canvas WxH replay both on one clock add --animate (HTML output)

--label-a / --label-b and --style-a / --style-b apply to the --animate replay too.

docs.title: Style keys
docs.text:
--style-a and --style-b take a comma-separated KEY=VALUE list and can be repeated. They are the app's Scanpath A / Scanpath B rows and compare_scanpaths's style_a / style_b. A key left out keeps that scanpath's default.

Key Value Left out fix_color #RRGGBB that scanpath's default saccade_color #RRGGBB that scanpath's default box_color #RRGGBB, the outline of that scanpath's word boxes its fix_color box_fill_color #RRGGBB, the boxes' fill --word-box-fill-color box_line_opacity, box_fill_opacity 0–1 --word-box-line-opacity, --word-box-fill-opacity raw_gaze_color #RRGGBB, that scanpath's raw-gaze samples its fix_color heatmap_colorscale a Plotly color scale; the range stays shared, and two different scales get a color bar each --heatmap-colorscale saccade_style solid, dash, dot or dashdot that scanpath's default saccade_width px that scanpath's default marker_size_range MIN:MAX that scanpath's default opacity 0–1 that scanpath's default hollow true or false that scanpath's default

The --animate replay draws one set of word boxes and no raw gaze, so it ignores the box_* keys and raw_gaze_color.

docs.title: What a comparison can't combine
docs.text:
• --compare-with cannot be combined with --all-screens or --screens. A comparison is one figure of two trials, each drawn from one screen. B's --compare-screen is looked up in B's trial, so it can be a later screen, or a screen of the second dataset.
  • An overlay of two datasets needs matching canvases. On two different canvases, --compare-layout overlay exits with an error, and so does --animate, which replays both scanpaths in one coordinate space. Use --compare-layout side-by-side or stacked, without --animate. Two screens of one dataset with different canvases are refused the same way. Nothing is rescaled.
  • Without --compare-canvas, the second dataset's screen size is estimated from its data, as A's is when neither --canvas nor a built-in source gives one. The data rarely spans the whole screen, so give both screen sizes when you know them.
  • A second dataset can only be loaded from files. In Python, compare_scanpaths takes B's frames directly, so any dataset you can load can be B.

docs.title: Raw gaze
docs.text:
--raw-gaze PATH… reads a Raw gaze table, with its columns auto-detected like --fixations, and draws the plotted trial's samples under the fixations. With --compare-with it covers both scanpaths, each in its scanpath's color. --compare-raw-gaze PATH… gives B's samples when B comes from another dataset. With the bundled demo, --sample-raw-gaze draws the recorded samples for the selected reading. --animate ignores raw gaze with a warning.

scanpath-studio render --sample -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_2_2_Adv --screen Paragraph \
  --sample-raw-gaze --raw-gaze-opacity 0.4 -o raw_gaze.html

To plot the same reading's pupil area over its recorded clock, use --x-field timestamp_ms --y-field pupil_area with --sample-raw-gaze. scanpath-studio check --sample includes the raw table and reports how many samples have missing positions.

When --raw-gaze is the only input, it is the dataset. --list-trials lists its trials, and render draws the chosen trial's samples as recorded. No fixations are detected from them, so --animate and --compare-with exit with an error that says so.

scanpath-studio render --raw-gaze gaze_samples.csv --list-trials
scanpath-studio render --raw-gaze gaze_samples.csv -t t3 -o samples.png

docs.title: Multipart trials and many trials
docs.text:
render writes one trial per run. For many figures, use the Python batch recipe or the Export bundle on the app's Export tab.

A multipart trial is the exception. --all-screens writes one __screen-001-<id> file per screen of the selected trial, and --screens Title,Paragraph writes only the screens named, each still numbered by its place in the trial. When your tables have no screen column, --trial-parts-manifest manifest.json assigns source rows to screens.

scanpath-studio render --words ia.csv --fixations fix.csv --list-parts
scanpath-studio render --words ia.csv --fixations fix.csv \
  -p p1 -t t3 --screen question -o question.svg
scanpath-studio render --words ia.csv --fixations fix.csv \
  -p p1 -t t3 --all-screens --animate --screen-transition recorded \
  -o replay.html

docs.title: When a column isn't recognized
docs.text:
Column names are auto-detected (EyeLink, Tobii, SMI, Pupil Labs, Gazepoint and snake_case spellings). When one isn't, render stops and prints which field it could not find, the names it looked for, the columns your table has, and a mapping to start from. Pass that mapping back as JSON, inline or as a path to a .json file, with --word-schema (the --words table) and/or --fix-schema (the --fixations table). check takes the same two flags.

scanpath-studio render --words ia.csv --fixations fix.csv \
  --word-schema '{"trial": "TRIAL_LABEL", "word_id": "IA_ID", "text": "IA_LABEL",
                  "left": "IA_LEFT", "right": "IA_RIGHT", "top": "IA_TOP", "bottom": "IA_BOTTOM"}' \
  --fix-schema fix_schema.json -o scanpath.html

A mapping replaces auto-detection for that table, so it has to name every required field, not only the one that failed. It is the same dict load_scanpath_data(word_schema=…, fix_schema=…) takes in Python. A second dataset's tables in a comparison take theirs as --compare-word-schema, --compare-fix-schema and --compare-raw-gaze-schema.

docs.title: render flags
docs.text: Every render flag, generated from the command's parser, with the defaults and help that --help prints. The figure flags are grouped like the figure options they set.

docs.title: Trial and output
docs.text: Option Value Default Description -p--participant PARTICIPANT — Participant ID (default: the first). -t--trial TRIAL — Trial ID (default: the participant's first). --screen SCREEN — Screen ID within a multipart trial (default: the first screen). --list-trials switch — Print every trial with its participant, trial and text IDs, then exit. Pass a trial ID to -t. --list-parts switch — Print the screens of each multipart trial in order, then exit. -p and -t narrow the list. --all-screens switch — Render every screen of the selected trial, one file each. The screen ID goes before the output's extension. --screens ID[,ID...] — Like --all-screens, for only these screens: comma-separated screen IDs, e.g. Title,Paragraph. See --list-parts. --screen-transition instant, recorded instant With --all-screens --animate: record no delay between screens (instant) or the recorded one (recorded) in each file's metadata (default: instant). -o--output PATH — Output file. Its extension sets the format: .html, .png, .svg or .pdf. --animate switch — Create a replay as interactive HTML or an editable publication project.

docs.title: Input
docs.text: Option Value Default Description --sample switch — Use the bundled demo, from OneStop: 2 participants, 12 trials each, every screen of a trial from title to feedback (--list-trials shows them; --screen picks one). --authoring PATH — A draft file from the app's Draw a scanpath screen. --words PATH [PATH ...] — The Words table: CSV, TSV, TXT, TAB, Parquet, Feather, XLSX or XLS, or a .zip of them. Columns are auto-detected from EyeLink, Gazepoint, Tobii, SMI, Pupil Labs and snake_case names. Several paths, or a quoted glob, are stacked into one table. --fixations PATH [PATH ...] — The Fixations table, in the formats --words reads and auto-detected the same way. Several paths, or a quoted glob, are stacked into one table (e.g. one file per participant). --image-root DIR — A folder of stimulus images. Each row's image is found with --image-pattern and stored in its image_path column. Add --show-stimulus-image to draw them. Works with every input, including --sample and the public datasets. --image-pattern PATTERN {text_id}.png File name pattern inside --image-root, with column placeholders, e.g. '{text_id}.png' or '{participant_id}/{trial_id}.png'. --trial-parts-manifest PATH — A JSON manifest that assigns source rows to the screens of each trial, in order. Use it with --words / --fixations when the tables have no screen column. --word-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --words table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. --fix-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --fixations table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. --keep-columns COLUMN [COLUMN ...] — More columns to keep through loading, under the names they have in your files (e.g. a pupil size), from whichever table has them. Without it, loading keeps only the mapped and recognized fields. A kept fixation column can be used by --color-by, an axis or a hover. Same as keep_columns= in api.load_scanpath_data. --potec DIR — Load the PoTeC corpus (DiLi-Lab/PoTeC) from DIR, downloading the files it needs (~45 MB) on first use. It has 75 participants, with IDs between 0 and 105 (--list-trials shows them). A trial is one participant reading one text, named <participant>_<text> (e.g. 0_b0). The texts are b0–b5 and p0–p5. --onestop DIR — Load the OneStop corpus from DIR. The public variant downloads the reports for the chosen regime and parts from OSF on first use, tens to hundreds of MB each. The lacclab variant reads a local export. Choose with --onestop-regime, --onestop-part and --onestop-variant. --onestop-regime ordinary, information_seeking, repeated, information_seeking_repeated ordinary OneStop reading regime for --onestop (default: ordinary). --onestop-part Title, Question_Preview, Paragraph, Questions, Answers, QA, Feedback — OneStop trial part for --onestop. Repeatable (default: Paragraph). With several, each part is a separate trial. --onestop-variant public, lacclab public OneStop source for --onestop: public, downloaded from OSF, or lacclab, a local lab-processed export with no download. --participant-metadata FILE [FILE ...] — A participant metadata table: one row per participant, with a participant ID column and any other fields. Several files, or a glob, are stacked into one table. Its rows are checked against the loaded participants and reported, and its fields are added to the --list-trials output. --trial-metadata FILE [FILE ...] — A trial metadata table: one row per trial, with a trial ID column and any other fields. Several files, or a glob, are stacked into one table. It is checked and reported the same way, and its fields are added to the --list-trials output. --trial-metadata-participant-column--trial-metadata-reader-column COLUMN — Key the --trial-metadata table by participant and trial, with this column as the participant ID. Without it, the table is keyed by trial ID alone, and each row applies to every participant's reading of that trial. This is never guessed from the file. --text-metadata FILE [FILE ...] — A text metadata table: one row per text, with a text ID column and any other fields. Several files, or a glob, are stacked into one table. It is checked and reported the same way, and its fields are added to the --list-trials output. It is keyed by text alone, never by participant.

docs.title: Fixations
docs.text: Option Value Default Description --no-fixations switch — Hide the fixations. --fixation-index switch — Number the fixations in order (the app's Fixation index). --no-fixation-index--no-order switch — Hide the fixation numbers (the default). --snap-fixations switch — Move each fixation up or down onto its text line: its word's line, else the nearest. Its x stays. --snap-position sets where on the line. --snap-position LINES — Where on its line a snapped fixation sits, in line heights from the line's middle: 0 centers it, -0.5 is the top edge, 0.5 the bottom edge (default: -0.5). Used with --snap-fixations. --palette {default,print,high-contrast} — Color palette (the app's Palette): default (colorblind-safe, Okabe–Ito), print (grayscale, for black-and-white printing) or high-contrast. The app's palette names work too. Each --*-color flag overrides it. --color-by FIELD — Fixations table column to color the fixations by, e.g. duration_ms, or 'line' for each fixation's text line (same as --color-by-line). Default: '(uniform)', one color, since marker size already shows duration. --fixation-color COLOR — Fixation color when --color-by is '(uniform)' (default: #0072B2). --fixation-symbol circle, square, diamond, triangle-up, cross, x, star, hexagon, heart — Fixation marker shape. Unlike color, shape survives a grayscale print (default: circle). --fixation-colorscale NAME — Color scale for --color-by, e.g. Viridis (default: Blues). --marker-size-range MIN MAX — Smallest and largest fixation marker size in px, e.g. 4 12 (default: 8 24). A smaller range suits thumbnails. --marker-size-scale sqrt, linear, log, relative — How duration sets marker size (default: sqrt). sqrt, linear and log map --marker-duration-range onto --marker-size-range, so a duration gets the same size in every trial, comparison and replay. With sqrt, marker area grows with duration. relative stretches each figure from its shortest to its longest fixation. --marker-duration-range LO HI — The durations in ms that get the smallest and largest marker (default: 50 600). Shorter and longer fixations are clamped to them. Not used by --marker-size-scale relative. --fixation-opacity O — Opacity of fixation markers, 0–1 (default: 0.7). --fixation-outline-width PX — Outline width around each filled fixation marker, 0–5 px; 0 draws none (default: 0.5). --fixation-outline-color COLOR — Color of that outline (default: #111111). --hollow-fixations switch — Draw the fixations as outlines instead of filled markers. --color-by-line switch — Color each fixation by the text line it lands on, with the lines found from the word boxes. Overrides --color-by. Same as --color-by line. --fixation-color-range LO HI — Fix the --color-by color scale to LO..HI instead of the trial's range, so several figures share one scale. --order-font-size PX — Size of the fixation index numbers (default: 10). --order-font-color COLOR — Color of the fixation index numbers for a single scanpath (default: #111111). --order-label-position above, inside, below — Where each fixation index number sits on its fixation (default: above). --no-fixation-colorbar switch — Leave out --color-by's color bar. --fixation-colorbar-orientation vertical, horizontal — Fixation color bar: beside the plot (vertical, default) or below it. --fixation-colorbar-tickangle DEG — Fixation color bar: tick-label angle, -90–90 (default: 0). --fixation-colorbar-tickfont-size PX — Fixation color bar: tick-label size (default: 12). --fixation-colorbar-thickness PX — Fixation color bar: thickness, 4–40 px (default: 14). --fixation-colorbar-length F — Fixation color bar: length as a share of the plot's side, 0.1–1.0 (default: a third of its height upright, 0.6 of its width lying down).

docs.text: Option Value Default Description --no-saccades switch — Hide the saccades. --saccade-arrows switch — Draw an arrowhead on each saccade (the app's Direction arrows). --saccade-color COLOR — Saccade line and arrow color, as hex or a CSS name (default: #CC79A7). --saccade-style solid, dash, dot, dashdot — Saccade line dash style (default: solid). --saccade-width PX — Saccade line width in px, 0.5–10 (default: 2). --saccade-arrow-size PX — Size of the --saccade-arrows arrowheads, 4–40 px (default: 12). --saccade-color-by-type switch — Color each saccade by its type: forward, skip, refixation, return sweep or regression (the app's By type). --saccade-color-by-direction switch — Color each saccade as forward or regression (the app's Forward / regression). --saccade-type-color CLASS=COLOR — Set one saccade type's color, e.g. --saccade-type-color regression=#000000. Repeatable. Types: forward, skip, refixation, return_sweep, regression. Implies --saccade-color-by-type. With --saccade-color-by-direction, it sets the forward and regression colors instead. --saccade-arcs switch — Draw saccades as upward arcs instead of straight lines (the app's Shape: Arc). --saccade-opacity O — Opacity of saccade lines and arrows, 0–1 (default: 1).

docs.title: Stimulus
docs.text: Option Value Default Description --no-text--no-labels switch — Hide the stimulus text. --highlight-column COLUMN — Boolean Words table column that marks the words to highlight (e.g. is_in_aspan, OneStop's answer span; default: none). --critical-span-style sets how they are drawn. --critical-span-style mark-text, mark-border, underline, none — How the --highlight-column words are marked: mark-text recolors them, mark-border outlines their boxes, underline underlines each word, none hides the marks (default: mark-text). --stimulus-image PATH — Draw an image (PNG or JPG) under the scanpath as the stimulus. It is sized to the PNG's pixel size, else to the canvas. Use --stimulus-image-size and --stimulus-image-origin to place a cropped image in fixation coordinates. --stimulus-image-size WxH — Stimulus image size in px, e.g. 1310x991 (default: the PNG's pixel size, else the canvas). Lower it so the fixations, saccades and word boxes stand out on a busy image. --show-stimulus-image switch — Draw each trial's stimulus image under the scanpath, from the image_path column of its rows, placed at image_x / image_y. --image-root fills that column, and --sample ships its images. --stimulus-image takes precedence. --text-color COLOR — Stimulus text color (default: #000000). --redact-text switch — Replace each word with a rounded block in the text color and hide its text in tooltips. In a comparison, each scanpath's boxes are outlined in its color instead. --word-box-line-opacity O — Word-box outline opacity, 0–1; 0 draws the fill only (default: 1). Below 1 the outline color must be #rrggbb, #rgb or rgb(r, g, b). --word-box-fill-color COLOR — Word-box fill color, drawn at --word-box-fill-opacity: #rrggbb, #rgb or rgb(r, g, b) (default: #646464). --word-box-fill-opacity O — Word-box fill opacity, 0–1; 0 draws outlines only (default: 0.05).

docs.title: Heatmap
docs.text: Option Value Default Description --heatmap switch — Draw the heatmap. --no-heatmap switch — Hide the heatmap (the default). --heatmap-metric COLUMN — What the heatmap colors by (the app's Color → By): the fixation duration column, under your file's name or as duration_ms, or counts for the fixation count. Default: duration_ms. --heatmap-style word-boxes, smoothed — Heatmap style: word-boxes tints each word box, smoothed blurs the fixations (default: word-boxes). --heatmap-sigma PX — Blur of --heatmap-style smoothed, as a Gaussian σ in px (default: 2% of the data's larger span, at least 8 px). --heatmap-colorscale NAME — Heatmap color scale, e.g. Greens (default: Blues). --heatmap-norm linear, log — Heatmap color scaling: linear (default) or log. Log keeps a few words with long dwell times from washing out the rest. --heatmap-opacity O — Heatmap opacity, 0.05–1.0 (default: 0.5 for word-boxes, or 0.35 for a trial with no word boxes; 0.45 for smoothed). --heatmap-range LO HI — Fix the heatmap's color scale to LO..HI instead of the trial's range. --word-heatmap-col COLUMN — With --heatmap, for a dataset with no fixations: tint each word box by this numeric Words table column, e.g. gpt2_surprisal, instead of its total fixation duration. --word-heatmap-title TEXT — Color-bar title for --word-heatmap-col (default: Value). --no-heatmap-colorbar switch — Leave out the heatmap's color bar. --heatmap-colorbar-orientation vertical, horizontal — Heatmap color bar: beside the plot (vertical, default) or below it. --heatmap-colorbar-tickangle DEG — Heatmap color bar: tick-label angle, -90–90 (default: 0). --heatmap-colorbar-tickfont-size PX — Heatmap color bar: tick-label size (default: 12). --heatmap-colorbar-thickness PX — Heatmap color bar: thickness, 4–40 px (default: 14). --heatmap-colorbar-length F — Heatmap color bar: length as a share of the plot's side, 0.1–1.0 (default: a third of its height upright, 0.6 of its width lying down).

docs.title: Raw gaze
docs.text: Option Value Default Description --raw-gaze PATH [PATH ...] — The Raw gaze table to draw under the fixations, in the formats --fixations reads and auto-detected the same way. Several paths, or a quoted glob, are stacked into one table. Drawn on static figures and --compare-with comparisons, where each scanpath's samples take its color, but not with --animate. As the only input it is the dataset: its trials are listed and drawn as recorded, and no fixations are detected from the samples. --no-raw-gaze switch — Load the --raw-gaze table but hide its layer, like turning off the app's Raw gaze switch. With raw gaze as the only input, the figure then shows no gaze. --sample-raw-gaze switch — With --sample, draw the recorded EyeLink gaze samples for the selected reading. --raw-gaze-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --raw-gaze table, replacing auto-detection, in the form --fix-schema takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized. --raw-gaze-color COLOR — Raw gaze sample color (default: #888888). In a comparison, each scanpath's samples are drawn in its color instead. --raw-gaze-marker-size PX — Raw gaze sample size, 1–12 px (default: 4). --raw-gaze-opacity O — Raw gaze sample opacity, 0.1–1.0 (default: 0.6).

docs.title: Filters & highlights
docs.text: Option Value Default Description --fix-index-range START:END — Draw only fixations START to END, counting from 1, both included, e.g. --fix-index-range 1:40. --animate then replays only that range. With --compare-with it applies to both scanpaths, unless --compare-fix-index-range sets B's. --fixation-flag SPEC — Highlight or hide one kind of fixation, like the app's Filters & highlights. Repeatable. SPEC is CATEGORY=MODE[,threshold_ms=N][,symbol=S][,color=#RRGGBB]. CATEGORY is short, long, oob (outside every word box) or blink. MODE is off, highlight or hide. threshold_ms applies to short and long only. hide removes the fixations from the figure only; measures and exports keep them. E.g. --fixation-flag short=hide,threshold_ms=80. --saccade-classes CLASSES — Draw only these saccade types, comma-separated, e.g. --saccade-classes regression,return_sweep. Types: forward, skip, refixation, return_sweep, regression, other (off the text). A hidden type loses its line and its arrow. Default: all.

docs.title: Axes

Implies --coordinate-grid. Leave it out for an automatic spacing of 1, 2 or 5 × 10ⁿ px. --coordinate-grid-font-size PX — Size of the coordinate grid's labels, 6–36 px (default: 18). --x-field FIELD — Horizontal axis of the static chart (default: x). Choose a numeric fixation field, @elapsed_seconds from the first recorded fixation, or a raw sample field such as timestamp_ms, sample_index, pupil_area or pupil_diameter. --y-field FIELD — Vertical axis of the static chart (default: y). docs.title: Title & labels

A flag you give still wins. --illustration-label auto, show, hide auto The Illustration label: auto adds it when the figure changes what the data shows (e.g. snapped fixations or arced saccades), show always adds it, and hide leaves it out (default: auto). --illustration-text TEXT — The Illustration label's text (default: "Illustration · <reasons>"). --title TEXT — A title on the figure. The figure grows to fit it.

docs.title: Hover fields
docs.text: Option Value Default Description --word-hover-fields FIELDS — Comma-separated word columns to show on hover, in order. --word-hover-fields-json JSON — Ordered JSON array of word column names. Use this for names containing commas, or pass '[]' to leave the tooltip empty. --fixation-hover-fields FIELDS — Comma-separated fixation columns to show on hover, in order. --fixation-hover-fields-json JSON — Ordered JSON array of fixation column names. Use this for names containing commas, or pass '[]' to leave the tooltip empty. --word-hover-measure FIELD — The reading measure a word's hover shows (default: total_fixation_duration_ms; '' for none).

docs.title: Legends
docs.text: Option Value Default Description --no-highlight-legend switch — Hide the Text highlight legend, which names the highlighted words. The words stay marked. --legend highlight=SPEC places it. --no-color-legend switch — Hide the Fixation colors legend, which lists the categories of a categorical --color-by and the highlighted fixations. The markers still draw. --no-saccade-type-legend switch — With --saccade-color-by-type: hide the Saccade types legend. The colored lines still draw. --legend SPEC — Place one legend. Repeatable. SPEC is KIND=POSITION[,ARRANGEMENT][,SIZE]. KIND is compare (Compare (A/B)), saccades (Saccade types), colors (Fixation colors), size-key (Fixation sizes) or highlight (Text highlight). POSITION is auto, or SPOT-outside or SPOT-inside, with SPOT one of top-left, top-center, top-right, left, right, bottom-left, bottom-center, bottom-right. Outside grows the figure, and left and right run down the side. ARRANGEMENT is stacked or side-by-side, and SIZE the text size in px. E.g. --legend saccades=right-outside,stacked,14. Each legend's switch still decides whether it is drawn. --duration-size-legend--no-duration-size-legend switch — Show reference circles labeled in milliseconds for the sqrt, linear or log fixation size scale (off by default).

docs.title: Animate
docs.text: Option Value Default Description --playback-speed X 1.0 Animation speed multiplier for --animate (default: 1.0 = real time). --no-autoplay switch — With --animate: start the replay paused. By default the HTML file starts playing when it opens. --anim-grid-step-ms MS — With --animate: one frame per MS of reading time (default: 100). A smaller step is smoother and makes a larger file. --anim-max-frames N — With --animate: at most N frames (default: 360). A trial too long for that many at --anim-grid-step-ms gets a wider step.

docs.title: Compare
docs.text: Option Value Default Description --compare-with PARTICIPANT:TRIAL — The second scanpath, B, as PARTICIPANT:TRIAL. The last colon separates the IDs. Use --compare-participant and --compare-trial when the trial ID contains a colon. B comes from the loaded dataset unless --compare-words / --compare-fixations load a second one. --compare-participant ID — B's participant ID, paired with --compare-trial. --compare-trial ID — B's trial ID, paired with --compare-participant. --compare-screen SCREEN_ID — B's screen in a multipart trial, looked up in B's trial (default: its first screen). --screen picks A's. Each scanpath is drawn from one screen. --compare-layout overlay, side-by-side, stacked overlay How A and B are arranged (default: overlay). Across two datasets, overlay needs canvases of the same size. Different canvases are refused, so use side-by-side or stacked for them. Matching canvases that a dataset did not record still overlay, with a warning. --compare-stimulus both, a, b both On an overlay, whose word boxes and text to draw (default: both). Two datasets' word boxes line up only when the text is the same. A two-scanpath replay shows B's text for 'b' and A's text for 'a' or 'both'. --label-a TEXT — Name of scanpath A in the legend and tooltips. Requires --compare-with and --label-b. --label-b TEXT — Name of scanpath B in the legend and tooltips. Requires --label-a. --compare-legend--no-compare-legend switch — Draw the Compare (A/B) legend, which names the two scanpaths. On by default; --no-compare-legend hides it. Also applies to --animate. --style-a SPEC — Style for scanpath A, repeatable: KEY=VALUE[,...]. Colors (#RRGGBB): fix_color, saccade_color, box_color (word-box outline; default fix_color), box_fill_color (default --word-box-fill-color), raw_gaze_color (default fix_color). Also heatmap_colorscale (default --heatmap-colorscale, on the shared range), saccade_style (solid|dash|dot|dashdot), saccade_width (px), marker_size_range (MIN:MAX), opacity (0–1), box_line_opacity / box_fill_opacity (0–1; default --word-box-line-opacity / --word-box-fill-opacity), hollow (true|false). E.g. --style-a fix_color=#D55E00,opacity=0.5. A two-scanpath replay uses the fixation and saccade styles. --style-b SPEC — Style for scanpath B, repeatable: KEY=VALUE[,...]. Colors (#RRGGBB): fix_color, saccade_color, box_color (word-box outline; default fix_color), box_fill_color (default --word-box-fill-color), raw_gaze_color (default fix_color). Also heatmap_colorscale (default --heatmap-colorscale, on the shared range), saccade_style (solid|dash|dot|dashdot), saccade_width (px), marker_size_range (MIN:MAX), opacity (0–1), box_line_opacity / box_fill_opacity (0–1; default --word-box-line-opacity / --word-box-fill-opacity), hollow (true|false). E.g. --style-b fix_color=#D55E00,opacity=0.5. A two-scanpath replay uses the fixation and saccade styles. --compare-fixation-flag SPEC — Filters & highlights for scanpath B only. Repeatable. Same SPEC as --fixation-flag, e.g. --compare-fixation-flag short=hide,threshold_ms=80. Replaces --fixation-flag for B. --compare-saccade-classes CLASSES — The saccade types scanpath B draws, comma-separated, named as in --saccade-classes. Replaces --saccade-classes for B. Not with --animate, which draws every type. --compare-fix-index-range START:END — Draw only fixations START to END of scanpath B, counting from 1, both included. Replaces --fix-index-range for B. --stimulus-image-b PATH — Scanpath B's stimulus image, for a side-by-side or stacked comparison across two datasets, where each panel draws its image. Sized and placed like --stimulus-image. --stimulus-image-size-b WxH — Size of --stimulus-image-b in px (default: the PNG's pixel size, else --compare-canvas, else --canvas). --stimulus-image-origin-b X,Y — Top-left corner of --stimulus-image-b in B's screen px (default: 0,0). --compare-words PATH [PATH ...] — The Words table for a second dataset, B's. Same formats and globbing as --words. --compare-fixations PATH [PATH ...] — The Fixations table for a second dataset, B's. Same formats and globbing as --fixations. --compare-raw-gaze PATH [PATH ...] — The Raw gaze table for the second dataset, drawn under B's scanpath. Same formats as --raw-gaze. With no second dataset, --raw-gaze already covers both scanpaths. --compare-word-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --compare-words table, replacing auto-detection. Same form as --word-schema. --compare-fix-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --compare-fixations table, replacing auto-detection. Same form as --fix-schema. --compare-raw-gaze-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --compare-raw-gaze table, replacing auto-detection. Same form as --raw-gaze-schema. --compare-dataset-name NAME Dataset B Name of the second dataset, used in the trace names (default: 'Dataset B'). --compare-canvas WxH — The second dataset's screen size in px, e.g. 1680x1050. Estimated from its data when left out. An overlay, or --animate with both scanpaths, checks it against --canvas.

docs.title: corpus
docs.text:
corpus renders a styled corpus figure from a tidy CSV you already have, as plot_corpus_figure does. For --kind profile the CSV needs word_id and value columns.

scanpath-studio corpus --input profile.csv --kind profile --output profile.svg

To draw an overview CSV, pass its grouping column with --series-col. For example, this draws participant means and their observed ranges from a summary whose ID column is named reader.

scanpath-studio corpus --input overview.csv --kind overview --series-col reader \
  --measure-label "Total fixation duration (ms)" -o overview.html
Option Value Default Description --input PATH required The CSV. profile reads word_id and the value column, plus optional lo and hi; distribution reads the value column; difference reads word_id and diff. Overview reads the group column (--series-col), the mean (--value-col), lo and hi. --kind overview, profile, distribution, difference required A corpus overview, per-word profile, distribution or difference profile. -o--output PATH required Output file; any extension save_figure writes (.html, .png, .svg, .pdf). --measure-label MEASURE_LABEL Value Axis and legend label for the value (default: Value). --series-col SERIES_COL series Group ID for an overview, or column naming the overlaid series (default: series). --value-col VALUE_COL value The value column (default: value). --percent switch — Show overview values and bounds stored as proportions (0–1) as percentages. --primary-color PRIMARY_COLOR — First series color (overview: #0072B2, other figures: #1f77b4). --secondary-color SECONDARY_COLOR #e45756 Second series color (default: #e45756).

docs.title: recipe
docs.text:
Recreate an Overview, Cohort profile or Difference word profile CSV from its downloaded JSON recipe and source tables. Recipes include the original column mappings. If raw gaze supplied the text IDs used by a metadata filter, pass its files with --raw-gaze. The command identifies any missing metadata or annotation input and verifies the regenerated CSV against the checksum in the recipe when available.

scanpath-studio recipe profile.recipe.json --words words.csv --fixations fixations.csv -o profile.csv

Positional arguments

Option Value Default Description RECIPE.json required Analysis recipe downloaded from Corpus Analysis.

Options

Option Value Default Description --sample switch — Use the bundled demo. --words WORDS [WORDS ...] — Original Words table(s). --fixations FIXATIONS [FIXATIONS ...] — Original Fixations table(s). --raw-gaze RAW_GAZE [RAW_GAZE ...] — Original raw gaze table(s) when a text metadata filter uses their IDs. --trial-parts-manifest TRIAL_PARTS_MANIFEST — Multipart trial manifest used at import. --word-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --words table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. --fix-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --fixations table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. --keep-columns COLUMN [COLUMN ...] — More columns to keep through loading, under the names they have in your files (e.g. a pupil size), from whichever table has them. Without it, loading keeps only the mapped and recognized fields. A kept fixation column can be used by --color-by, an axis or a hover. docs.title: check
docs.text:
check runs the Data Management page's Data checks on your tables without opening the app. It looks for:

  • fixations lasting 0 ms or less, or with an infinite duration or onset;
  • fixations and raw gaze samples with no finite position, or one more than a million pixels off the screen;
  • word boxes with no area, or no finite position or size within a million pixels;
  • screen sizes that are not finite and positive.

Each finding gives the rows and trials affected, a few example rows, and what the app does with them. check changes nothing and exits 0 whatever it finds. --json prints the table check_data_health returns. In example rows, missing values are null and infinite values are the strings "Infinity" or "-Infinity". To save a QC record, use --json-report. Its tables object counts the source rows read, the rows with usable identifiers, and the normalized rows checked. Stimulus words shared across readings can expand into more checked rows. The report distinguishes empty tables, blank rows and rows with missing participant or trial IDs. Its findings list matches --json.

scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv
scanpath-studio check --raw-gaze gaze_samples.csv --json

Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. --fix-schema JSON — Column mapping for the --fixations table, replacing auto-detection. A JSON object from each field to a column name, or the path of a JSON file holding one, e.g. '{"trial": "TRIAL_INDEX", "word_id": "IA_ID", ...}'. It is the dict api.load_scanpath_data takes. Needed only when a column isn't recognized, and the error then prints a mapping to start from. --keep-columns COLUMN [COLUMN ...] — More columns to keep through loading, under the names they have in your files (e.g. a pupil size), from whichever table has them. docs.title: add
docs.text:
add adds your tables to the app's dataset list, as Add dataset does, without opening the app. Run scanpath-studio afterwards and the app opens on the new dataset. If the app is already open, reload its browser tab right away: changes you make in it before the reload are not saved. It works for an app on your own computer, not a hosted one.

scanpath-studio add "Pilot 3" --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv --canvas 1920x1080
scanpath-studio add "Pilot 3" --fixations fixations_v2.csv --replace

A name that is already saved is an error unless you pass --replace, which swaps the dataset's tables and keeps its annotations, metadata tables, share links, description and recording setup (unless you give a new description or --canvas). Without --canvas, the app uses a screen the data records, or estimates one from the extent of the data. In Python, use add_dataset.

docs.title: remove
docs.text:
remove takes a dataset you added, in the app or with add, off the app's dataset list. Its annotations, metadata tables and description go with it, as its Remove on the Data Management page does. Built-in and public datasets can't be removed. If the app last had it open, it next opens on its default dataset.

scanpath-studio remove "Pilot 3"
scanpath-studio remove "Pilot 3" --missing-ok   # no error if it isn't there

In Python, use remove_dataset.

Positional arguments

Option Value Default Description NAME required The name the dataset list shows (case does not matter).

Options

Option Value Default Description --missing-ok switch — Exit quietly when no dataset has the name, instead of with an error.

docs.title: open
docs.text:
open opens the app on a dataset you added, or one the app has itself (the bundled demo, a public corpus), at one reading, with the figure set by the same flags render takes. If the app is running on this computer, the link opens in your browser. Otherwise open starts the app and opens the link once it is up. --print prints the link instead.

scanpath-studio open "Pilot 3" -p p07 -t t12
scanpath-studio open "Pilot 3" -p p07 -t t12 --heatmap --saccade-style dash --print

The link is the one Share → Link writes for the same view. Settings it leaves out keep the values the app has. It names the dataset, so a dataset you added opens only where it was added. A link carries no file: render's input, output and --stimulus-image flags are refused, and --show-stimulus-image draws the dataset's own pages. In Python, use app_link.

Positional arguments

Option Value Default Description NAME required The dataset's name in the app's list.

Options

Option Value Default Description -p--participant PARTICIPANT — Participant ID. -t--trial TRIAL — Trial ID (without it, the participant's first trial). --screen SCREEN — Screen ID within a trial recorded over several screens. --animate switch — Open the replay of the reading. --port PORT 8501 The port the app listens on, or is started on (default: 8501). --print switch — Print the link and exit, without opening or starting anything.

docs.title: annotations
docs.text:
annotations reads and writes the favorites, tags and notes on a dataset you added. export writes the same annotations.json as Data Management → Annotations → Export, or a CSV table with one row per annotated reading. import reads either: a CSV needs participant_id and trial_id, optionally screen_id, and any of favorite, tags (separated by ;, so a tag can't contain one in a CSV) and note. Importing adds a reading's tags to the ones it has, and a favorite or note in the file replaces its own; a blank stays as it was. This differs from the app's Import, which keeps or swaps a reading's whole entry. --replace makes the dataset's annotations exactly the file's, and is refused when none of the file's readings is in the dataset. Readings the dataset does not have are listed and left out. If the app is open, reload its browser tab to see the new ones.

scanpath-studio annotations import "Pilot 3" qc_flags.csv
scanpath-studio annotations export "Pilot 3" -o annotations.json

In Python, use write_annotations and read_annotations.

docs.title: annotations export
docs.text:
Positional arguments

Option Value Default Description NAME required The name the dataset list shows (case does not matter).

Options

Option Value Default Description -o--output FILE required The file to write, .json or .csv.

docs.title: annotations import
docs.text:
Positional arguments

Option Value Default Description NAME required The name the dataset list shows (case does not matter). FILE required The .json or .csv file to read.

Options

Option Value Default Description --replace switch — Make the dataset's annotations exactly the file's, instead of adding the file's to them. Refused when none of the file's readings is in the dataset, so a file made for another dataset deletes nothing.

docs.title: cache
docs.text:
A local or desktop run saves your session on your computer, so a refresh or a restart resumes where you left off. It saves uploaded datasets, column mappings, view settings, saved designs, metadata tables and annotations. cache shows what is stored and can delete it.

scanpath-studio cache            # datasets, rows, size, folder, last written
scanpath-studio cache --path     # just the folder
scanpath-studio cache --json     # the same status as JSON
scanpath-studio cache --clear    # delete the recovery cache
Option Value Default Description --path switch — Print the cache folder and exit. --json switch — Print the status as JSON. --clear switch — Delete the recovery cache.

Open Data Management → Saved work → Your session to see the same information. A running app writes a new copy at its next change, so clear the cache with the app closed.

To Use turn caching off for one launch scanpath-studio --no-persist turn it off wherever the variable is set SCANPATH_STUDIO_PERSIST=0 move the folder SCANPATH_STUDIO_STATE_DIR

Hosted deployments do not cache by default.

docs.title: version
docs.text:
version says which build this is and how it was installed. --check also asks GitHub whether a newer release is out and says how to update your install. Only --check uses the network.

scanpath-studio version           # the build, and how it was installed
scanpath-studio version --check   # …and whether a newer release is out
Option Value Default Description --check switch — Ask GitHub for the latest release and say how to update this install. --timeout SECONDS 5.0 How long to wait for GitHub, in seconds (default: 5).

Between releases the version names the build: 0.35.0.post3+g8f18219 is three commits after 0.35.0, at commit 8f18219. In a local install or the desktop app, open Help → About & citation → App details → :material:update: Check for updates. In Python, call check_for_updates.

docs.title: cite
docs.text:
cite prints how to cite Scanpath Studio. --corpus adds the citation of the public corpus you used.

scanpath-studio cite                           # BibTeX
scanpath-studio cite --format apa --corpus onestop
scanpath-studio cite --format credit           # one sentence for a figure caption
Option Value Default Description --format bibtex, apa, ris, csl-json, credit bibtex Bibtex (default), apa, ris (Zotero, Mendeley, EndNote), csl-json, or credit: one sentence to paste into a figure caption. --corpus onestop, potec — Add this public corpus's citation after the software's.

You don't have to add the citation to your files by hand: every figure render writes carries it in its file metadata. The same entries are cite in Python.

docs.title: The fixations don't line up with the text
docs.text:
Words and fixations must use the same pixel coordinates and share trial IDs. If the fixations are shifted, mirrored or scaled relative to the words, check that both tables use the same origin, units and offsets. Correct any coordinate differences before importing the tables (What your data needs → Files and units).

If the fixations sit on the words but the figure is framed or sized wrongly, set the screen resolution of the monitor used in the experiment. Open Data Management → Current dataset → Edit dataset → Recording setup and choose Screen → I know it. Estimate from my data gives only a lower bound.

docs.title: The text is too big or too small
docs.text: The text is drawn to scale from the word boxes and the recording screen size. Set the real resolution first (see above). For OneStop it is 2560×1440, and in Python you pass canvas_size=(2560, 1440). If the text is still off, set the line spacing under Recording setup → Text size → Fit to word boxes, or line_spacing= in Python. Line spacing is the distance between lines, in font sizes.

docs.title: A column was detected wrongly
docs.text: The app guesses columns from their names. Pick the right one under Data Management → Current dataset → Edit dataset, or pass word_schema / fix_schema to load_scanpath_data.

docs.title: Can I load only one table?
docs.text: Yes. A Words table alone shows the text and any reading measures it carries. A Fixations table alone shows the fixations without the text. A Raw gaze table can also be the only table. Most features need both words and fixations. When your tables cover different trials, the app lists every trial found in any table and draws the layers available for it.

docs.title: Can I open PoTeC or OneStop in the online demo?
docs.text: No. The online demo has only the bundled demo, and it doesn't download public datasets. In the desktop app or a pip install, each public dataset downloads once, with one click, and stays on your computer.

docs.title: My zip file is refused as too large
docs.text: The app limits how far a .zip may decompress: 32 GB per file and 64 GB in total. The error names the setting that raises the limit, for example SCANPATH_ZIP_MAX_MEMBER_GB=64 scanpath-studio.

docs.title: Does the app compute reading measures?
docs.text: No. Corpus Analysis and Export show the reading measures in your Words table, as your eye-tracking software defines them (Reading measures).

docs.title: Does  Filters & highlights change my data?
docs.text: No. It changes only what the figure draws. Your tables and measures stay as they are.

docs.title: Image or video export fails
docs.text: These exports need Chrome, Chromium or Edge on the computer that runs Scanpath Studio: PDF, GIF and MP4 files, static images from Python or the CLI, and export bundles with images. Installing one of these browsers is enough. With a pip install you can instead run plotly_get_chrome -y once. HTML files, and the current figure's PNG and SVG, work without a browser.

docs.title: Can someone else open my share link?
docs.text: Yes, but the link does not contain your data, so they need to load the same dataset first. The bundled demo opens directly. A public dataset opens if they have it set up.

docs.title: Where does my data go?
docs.text: When you run Scanpath Studio locally or as the desktop app, your data stays on your computer. There are no accounts, and scanpath-studio and the desktop app send no usage statistics. The online demo runs on Streamlit Community Cloud, whose page around the app has its own analytics (privacy policy). See Your data for what a local install saves, where, and how to clear it.

docs.title: Can I share a figure without showing the text?
docs.text: Yes. Turn on Stimulus ▾ → Text → Redact. Each word becomes a rounded block over its letters, so the figure keeps the layout of the text but none of its words. Hovers and saved HTML hide the words too. Also turn off the stimulus image, since it shows the screen as it was. On the command line, use render --redact-text, and in Python redact_text=True. The data tables and exported tables still hold the words.

docs.title: Will a refresh lose my work?
docs.text:
Local and desktop installs normally save your datasets and settings between visits. Open Data Management → Saved work → Your session to check whether saving is on. The online demo keeps uploads only for the current session. Before refreshing, export your annotations and settings.

If the files of one saved dataset go missing or are damaged, the rest of the session still comes back. The app names the dataset it could not restore, keeps that saved copy unchanged, and offers Retry and Remove saved copy. Saved metadata tables that can't be read are kept the same way. If the whole saved copy can't be read, the app opens without it and stops saving over it until you retry or clear it.

If two tabs use the same local recovery folder, edits to different trial annotations can be saved together. When a save would overwrite newer work, the older tab shows a warning and keeps your edits open. Copy or export them before reloading that tab. To save your notes, open Data Management → Current dataset → Annotations for the dataset and download the JSON file.

docs.title: How do I stop saving, or delete what is saved?
docs.text: Start the app with scanpath-studio run --no-persist to save nothing. To delete your saved session, open Data Management → Saved work → Your session → Saved session details → Clear saved session…, or close the app and run scanpath-studio cache --clear. That leaves the public datasets you downloaded: delete one with its button under Dataset downloads. See Your data and Recovery cache.

docs.title: Where do I ask a question, report a bug or send feedback?
docs.text: Help → Troubleshooting & feedback has short answers in the app. To contact the project, ask a question in Q&A, report a bug, or suggest an improvement in Ideas. Report a bug gives you the version and system details to copy. In a terminal, scanpath-studio --version prints the version.

docs.title: How do I update Scanpath Studio?
docs.text:
In a local install or the desktop app, open Help → About & citation → App details → Check for updates. In the desktop app, choose Update & restart. For a Python install, run:

pip install -U scanpath-studio

docs.title: Will my links, settings and scripts work after an update?
docs.text: Not necessarily. Until version 1.0, any release may change the app, its share links and saved settings, the Python API and the CLI. The changelog lists the changes in each release. To reproduce a result, note the version you used and install that one: pip install scanpath-studio==<version>.

docs.title: How do I cite Scanpath Studio?
docs.text: See Cite Scanpath Studio for BibTeX and APA entries, and Bundled demo for the bundled demo's source. In the app, Cite under each download gives the same entries, and every exported file carries the citation in its metadata (Cite what you export).

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
• Desktop app Recommended

    No coding required. Your data stays on your computer.

    macOS Windows Linux

    Setup details & other downloads
    • macOS 14+, Apple silicon: open the DMG, drag to Applications, then launch. If blocked: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Open Anyway. Intel Mac or older macOS? Use Python below.
    • Windows: run the installer, then launch from Start. If SmartScreen warns: More info → Run anyway. A portable ZIP is also available.
    • Linux: extract, then run ./ScanpathStudio/ScanpathStudio.

    All downloads

  • Try online

    Explore the bundled demo without installing anything.

    Launch demo

  • Install with Python

    Requires Python 3.11–3.15. Runs on your computer and opens in your browser.

    pip install scanpath-studio
scanpath-studio

docs.title: Try the Dev build
docs.text:
Stable is the published release on PyPI and the desktop downloads above. Dev follows the changes merged into main. You can open the Dev app or run it locally. In a separate Python environment with Git installed, run:

python -m pip install "git+https://github.com/lacclab/scanpath-studio.git@dev"
scanpath-studio

Help shows which channel you are running. Its release notes are in About & citation → App details.

For a Git installation, the update command keeps your repository, requested ref and package subdirectory. An install from an official release tag follows the Stable channel for updates. If you selected a commit hash, choose the new revision in your original install command when you are ready to move.

docs.title: Replay a sample reading
docs.text:
On your first visit, the app opens a reading from the OneStop demo. Choose Replay this reading to follow the reader’s fixations over the text. Press Pause, then Next fixation to step through the recording. You can return to the sample walkthrough from Help → Task guides.

To work with your own recording, choose Import my data or follow Add your own data.

docs.title: Your first figure
docs.text:
Choose a reading in the demo to explore and save as an interactive figure.

  • 1 · Open a reading

    In the Scanpath View, choose Bundled demo in Select dataset. Then choose a reading in Select trial.

  • 2 · Choose a view

    Choose Heatmap to see where fixation time concentrates, or Scanpath to follow the order of fixations. Both tiles sit under Presets in Essentials and Full.

  • 3 · Save your figure

    In the Export tab under the plot, find Current figure. Set Download format to HTML, then click ⬇ Download HTML. Open the saved file in your browser to zoom and hover over the figure.
