docs.title: Export and share
docs.text: Save a figure, export many trials at once, or reuse a view in the app or in code.

docs.title: In the app
docs.text:
Goal Where Save the figure or replay on screen Export → Current figure Prepare a figure for a paper or slide Export → Prepare figure for export Export many trials and their tables Export → Export bundle Share a view or copy its code Share → Link or Code Reuse the figure settings My presets, or Share → Settings file

To export multiple trials, switch to Full and open Export bundle. Essentials offers Current figure for the figure or replay on screen.

For step-by-step instructions, see the export tutorials.

docs.title: Prepare a paper figure or slide
docs.text:
Open Scanpath → Export → Prepare figure for export. The preview shows the current reading, comparison or replay still. For a corpus chart, open Prepare figure for export directly beneath the chart. Choose Download PNG for a slide or document, or switch the file format to SVG, PDF or TIFF.

  • Crop lets you draw a rectangle, select a word span when words are available, or use the scanpath’s current zoom. Under Label events, pin a fixation or saccade and drag its label into position.
  • Caption and description suggests a caption and alternative text. Edit them, download both as text, or include the caption below the artwork.
  • For a replay, Replay clip lets you choose the interval, speed and poster frame. Prepare MP4 and poster produces a ZIP with the clip, poster and editable file. Rendering PDF or video in the app requires Chromium on the server.
  • When a journal specifies dimensions, open Print settings to set the width, resolution or minimum text size. In Full mode on the Scanpath View, Use this size for batch export prints each bundle figure at the prepared artwork’s width and resolution; the crop, labels and caption stay with the prepared figure.

Under Save or open, save a copy on this device or download an editable file for a coauthor. The file includes the plotted data, tooltip fields and embedded images. Open it here, under Data Management → Saved work → Saved figures, or via Share → Settings file. A Share link opens the editor on the source view. An editable file also restores your crop, labels and caption. Older files containing several figures open with their saved layout.

docs.title: Reproduce a coauthor's results
docs.text:
The installed package includes a fictional three-reader study, its raw tables, recording setup, one tagged exclusion, figure settings and a cohort recipe. To work through it in an empty folder, copy the example and follow its README.

python -c "from importlib.resources import files; from shutil import copytree; copytree(files('scanpath_studio') / 'sample_data' / 'coauthor', 'canal-study')"

The commands recreate a figure and a two-word results table. A checksum from the original release lets the recipient verify the table byte for byte.

docs.title: Cite what you export
docs.text:
Files saved through Export include citation information in their metadata. To add a visible credit to the figure, use Figure → Title & labels → Credit.

  • Cite, under each download and in Share → Code, gives a one-line figure credit, the APA reference and BibTeX, and .bib and .ris files for Zotero, Mendeley or EndNote. For the bundled demo, OneStop or PoTeC, it cites the corpus too.
  • Each export bundle includes CITATION.bib and citation instructions in README.md.
  • Figure → Title & labels → Credit adds a small Made with Scanpath Studio line under the plot, for a figure shared without its caption. In code, pass show_credit=True, or --credit to render.
  • In code, cite and scanpath-studio cite print the citation.

A link can find an imported dataset on the same computer after you rename it. On another computer, import the sender’s data under the name in the link. The link checks that the recording tables match, including those for a second imported dataset in a comparison. Older links can open without checking the tables. All controls → Under the plot says what the recipient needs.

docs.title: Reproduce a figure
docs.text:
Open Share → Code and copy the Python or CLI code. It includes the figure's settings and your column mapping. The compact code includes changes that affect this view. For example, a comparison uses each scanpath's own fixation color for its index numbers. Select Show every option to include the other accepted figure settings. For a dataset you imported, replace the placeholder file paths with your own. Render in code shows a minimal example.

For a PNG at print size, pass width_mm and dpi to save_figure, or --width-mm and --dpi to render. To edit the layers in a vector editor, save each layer to a separate file with save_figure_layers or render --separable-layers. In the app's export bundle, this is Layers as separate files.

docs.title: Batch export
docs.text:
In the app, Export bundle → Trials to include picks the trials: This trial, All filtered trials, All trials of one participant, All trials of one text or All trials, ignoring filters. Open Preview bundle contents to see the selected readings, their filenames and the columns in their tables. A word-measures CSV can contain the original stimulus words even when the figure masks them. When you select specific screens, the bundle includes notes on those screens and their parent trials.

When you export all screens, rows with no Screen ID are included once in the trial’s tables. Selecting specific screens includes only rows assigned to those screens. A screen with raw gaze alone has its own sample table.

If a figure fails, the download includes the files that succeeded. With the same data and settings still open, choose Retry failed figure files. The app retries each missing format or layer and keeps the successful files. If it could not split a figure into layers, it tries that step again. Check index.csv for any files that still failed. Stopping a retry leaves the previous download available.

CSV bundles include columns.json and an editable read_csv.R. In R, set the working directory to the extracted bundle and run source("read_csv.R") with the jsonlite package installed. The example preserves reader IDs such as 01 and 1 as text. A blank measurement becomes NA and zero stays zero.

For a scripted batch, loop over the trial list.

Python: one HTML figure per trial 
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
out = Path("figures")
out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)

for pid, tid in sps.list_trials(words, fixations).itertuples(index=False):
    # Each demo reading has several screens; this saves its paragraph.
    fig = sps.plot_scanpath(words, fixations, pid, tid, screen="Paragraph")
    sps.save_figure(fig, out / f"{pid}_{tid}.html")

Use the data loaders for your own files. The CLI's render writes one trial per run.

docs.title: Replay export
docs.text:
With Animation selected, Export → Current figure saves the replay as HTML, GIF or MP4. In a saved HTML replay, Previous fixation and Next fixation move to individual onsets and show the fixation’s duration and assigned word when available. The time slider scrubs through the whole reading. Each frame of a GIF or MP4 shows the state reached at that frame’s start, and the last frame shows the complete scanpath. With a low frame cap, a fixation that begins between two frames first shows in the later one.

The CLI’s render --animate saves interactive HTML. For a GIF or MP4 in Python:

Python: save a GIF or MP4 
from pathlib import Path

import scanpath_studio as sps
from scanpath_studio.animation_export import export_animation

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
replay = sps.animate_scanpath(
    words, fixations, "l37_273", "l37_273_2_1_1_Ele", screen="Paragraph"
)
Path("replay.mp4").write_bytes(export_animation(replay, fmt="mp4"))

Use fmt="gif" and a .gif filename for GIF output.

Export setup and troubleshooting · Python save options · CLI options

docs.title: Proof two manuscript panels
docs.text:
In Compare, choose two readings with the same screen dimensions and a side-by-side or stacked layout. In Export → Current figure → Manuscript panel proof, enter the total print width. The proof shows the resulting label sizes in points and the numeric color limits shared by the two panels. Use the Fixations or Heatmap controls to choose your own limits.

Prepare manuscript SVG provides the lettered vector panels at that physical width. Save panel settings preserves their order, styles, width and selected limits. Open the settings file in Share → File, replace one reading and prepare the revised SVG.

docs.title: Data Management
docs.text: Load your own data, open a public dataset, or try the bundled demo.

docs.title: Choose a dataset
docs.text:
Pick a dataset in Select dataset above the plot or open Dataset library on the Data Management page.

  • Bundled demo includes 24 readings by two L1 English readers of 12 OneStop texts. Each reading keeps every screen the reader saw: the article's title (first paragraph only), the question preview, the paragraph, the question, the answers and the feedback. Each screen shows the experiment's own stimulus image, placed where the experiment drew it. The 1,000 Hz EyeLink samples cover each screen from its onset to the response that ended it. Each sample keeps its timestamp, screen coordinates, pupil area in tracker units and tracked eye. During tracking loss the coordinates and the pupil area are blank.
  • Hand-drawn sample: a scanpath drawn by hand over a short English text, which you can edit.
  • Public datasets: OneStop and PoTeC. In the desktop app or a pip install, each downloads the first time you open it.
  • + → Import files: your own tables.
  • + → Draw a scanpath: write a text and place its fixations by hand.

docs.title: Draw a scanpath
docs.text:
Choose + → Draw a scanpath, then type your passage. In Draw mode, click the words in reading order. Click a word twice for two visits, or click the space between words for a fixation without a target. For a regular sequence, Reset to one fixation per word places a 220 ms fixation on each word.

Use Select & move to drag a marker. The Fixation list lets you select visits that land on top of one another. Change Duration (ms) and use Play preview to check the timing. The Fixation table also accepts keyboard edits. Leaving both coordinates empty places the fixation at the center of its target word.

Save dataset opens the figure. To revise it, go to Data Management and click Edit drawing beside its name. Save changes updates the drawing, and Save as copy keeps a separate version. For another computer, download the editable draft from Share and open it with Load a saved draft in the drawing editor.

docs.title: OneStop
docs.text: The bundled demo comes from OneStop Eye Movements (Berzak et al., 2025), an English corpus with 360 participants. The full corpus is available as four public datasets: OneStop · Ordinary reading, OneStop · Information seeking, OneStop · Repeated reading and OneStop · Information seeking (repeated). Each downloads once from OSF.

docs.title: What your data needs
docs.text:
Start with a Fixations, Words or Raw gaze table. You can add the other tables whenever you need them.

To try a right-to-left passage, import the bundled sample_data/mixed_script_words.csv and sample_data/mixed_script_fixations.csv. The two synthetic lines combine Hebrew, Arabic, English, digits and punctuation. Use an 800 × 250 px canvas to see the recorded layout. The tenth fixation revisits the Arabic word on the second line.

Table Contents Fixations One row per fixation: trial ID, duration, and x/y or a word ID Words (interest areas) One row per word: trial ID, word ID and word box Raw gaze One row per gaze sample: trial ID, x and y Participants One row per participant, with metadata Trials One row per trial, with metadata Texts One row per text, with metadata

The app recognizes column names from common eye-tracker exports. Check the mapping when you import. To keep condition labels and other columns, pick them under Extra fields to keep. You can filter, sort and group trials by any metadata field.

docs.title: Files and units
docs.text:
• CSV, TSV, TXT, Parquet, Feather, Excel, or a ZIP of these files
  • Positions in pixels
  • Times in milliseconds. A time column whose header names its unit, such as [s], [μs] or [ns], is converted.
  • Word boxes as x/y/width/height or EyeLink's IA_LEFT/RIGHT/TOP/BOTTOM
  • Word IDs as numbers, or as text such as w1. Text IDs must match exactly in the Fixations and Words tables. With text IDs, the order of the rows in the Words table sets the word order.
  • Several files for one table, such as one file per trial, are stacked into one table, with each file's name in a source_file column. When an ID is only in the file name, use Derive columns from text to extract it into a column you can map. When you click Apply, a derived column named like an ID, such as participant, trial or stimulus, fills that ID field if it is empty.
  • Trial and Text IDs are matched exactly, so spell them the same way in both tables, including upper and lower case. The import screen says when they differ only in case.
  • Words tables with one box per character, as in Chinese or Japanese: turn on Merge character boxes into word boxes. The import screen suggests it when a word's rows are at different positions.

docs.title: Trials over several screens
docs.text: Map the Screen ID field in your tables. A column named screen_index sets the order of the screens. Without one, the screens are ordered by where they first appear, using the Fixations table if available. The app draws one screen at a time.

docs.title: Reading measures
docs.text: Corpus Analysis uses the per-word reading measures in your Words table, such as first fixation duration or total fixation duration. Map them when you import. EyeLink's IA_* columns are detected.

docs.title: Add your own data
docs.text:
For a walkthrough inside the import wizard, choose Setup help → Show setup guide.

  1. Choose + → Import files and name the dataset.
  2. Upload your tables and check the column mapping.
  3. Under Recording setup, enter the Screen, Monitor width and Text size if you know them.
  4. Optionally, in the desktop app or a local install, attach the stimulus images from a folder.
  5. Click Add dataset, then Open in Scanpath View to see its first trial. You can also open the figure from Data Management → Current dataset.

To import similar files again, click Download setup file before Add dataset. Next time, choose Start from → A setup file and upload your tables: the column mapping, derived columns, character-box merge and recording setup are filled in.

docs.title: Load and inspect in code
docs.text:
Load the same files in a script. The loaders detect column names the same way the app does.

Python and CLI PythonCLI 
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_scanpath_data("ia.csv", "fixations.csv")
print(sps.list_trials(words, fixations))

scanpath-studio render --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv --list-trials
scanpath-studio check --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv

For raw gaze, metadata and explicit column mappings, see the loaders and CLI input options.

docs.title: Add a dataset from a script
docs.text:
On your own computer, a script can add a dataset to the app's list. Use it to prepare the tables in code and then look at them in the app. Start the app afterwards and it opens on the new dataset. If the app is already open, reload its browser tab right away: changes you make in it before the reload are not saved.

PythonCLI 
import scanpath_studio as sps

sps.add_dataset(
    "Pilot 3",
    words="ia.csv",
    fixations="fixations.csv",
    canvas_size=(1920, 1080),
)

scanpath-studio add "Pilot 3" --words ia.csv --fixations fixations.csv --canvas 1920x1080

The tables load as load_scanpath_data loads them, and the dataset is saved with your other saved work. Adding again under the same name is an error unless you pass replace=True (--replace). That swaps the tables and keeps the dataset's annotations, metadata tables, share links, description and recording setup, unless you give a new description or screen. Without a screen size, the app uses one the data records, or estimates one from the extent of the data. To set it later, use Edit dataset. See add_dataset for every option.

To open the app on one reading of it, with the figure you want, write a link. It names the dataset, the participant and trial, and the figure in plot_scanpath's options or render's flags. From the CLI, open opens it in your browser, and starts the app first if it isn't running.

PythonCLI 
url = sps.app_link("Pilot 3", "p07", "t12", show_heatmap=True)

scanpath-studio open "Pilot 3" -p p07 -t t12 --heatmap

The link is the one Share → Link writes for that view, so settings it leaves out keep the values the app has. See app_link and open.

To take a dataset off the list again, use remove_dataset or scanpath-studio remove "Pilot 3". Any dataset you added can be removed this way, with its annotations and metadata tables, as its Remove on the Data Management page does.

docs.title: Annotations from a script
docs.text:
A script can also read and write the favorites, tags and notes on a dataset you added. A quality-control script can tag the readings it flags, and reviewers find them in the app with the tag filter. An analysis can read back what the reviewers marked.

PythonCLI 
import pandas as pd
import scanpath_studio as sps

flags = pd.DataFrame(
    {"participant_id": ["p01", "p02"], "trial_id": ["3", "7"], "tags": "Short"}
)
result = sps.write_annotations("Pilot 3", flags)
print(result.unknown)  # readings the dataset does not have, left out

marked = sps.read_annotations("Pilot 3")
excluded = marked[marked["tags"].map(lambda tags: "To exclude" in tags)]

scanpath-studio annotations import "Pilot 3" flags.csv
scanpath-studio annotations export "Pilot 3" -o annotations.csv

The table has one row per reading: participant_id, trial_id, screen_id for one screen of a trial recorded over several, and any of favorite, tags and note. In a CSV file, separate tags with ;. The app's exported annotations.json works too. Writing adds a reading's tags to the ones it has, and a favorite or note you give replaces its own. Pass mode="replace" (--replace) to make the dataset's annotations exactly the ones given; it is refused when none of the given readings is in the dataset. A reading the dataset does not have is left out and listed. An app already open shows the new annotations once its browser tab is reloaded. See write_annotations for every option.

docs.title: Manage datasets
docs.text:
Current dataset opens on Overview. It shows how many participants, trials and texts are in your selection and the average number of trials per participant. Fixation and word averages count trials that contain those rows. Eye-tracking data shows the row and trial counts for each table. Scanpath trial filters apply to these counts.

Click a table name to jump to its rows. Tables shows fixations, words, raw gaze samples, participants, trials and texts on one page. When you attach a participant, trial or text metadata file, that table shows the complete file.

Data checks looks for unusable values in the whole dataset, including trials outside the filters. Annotations lets you review, import and export the dataset’s favorites, tags and notes. A script can read and write them too; see Annotations from a script.

To switch datasets, open Dataset library. Search by name or filter by source, then click a dataset to open its overview. Saved work shows what will reopen next time. On a local install, Dataset downloads lists the public datasets on disk and lets you choose where future downloads go.

Use Edit dataset to change its name, column mapping, recording setup or metadata, then click Save changes. Download setup file saves the mapping, recording setup and character-box merge, so you can apply them to similar data.

The editor offers only the columns kept when the dataset was added. To use a column that isn't listed, remove the dataset and add it again from its files, mapping the column or keeping it under Extra fields to keep.

Under Data checks, Compare with planned trials (optional) accepts a CSV with participant_id and trial_id. Add screen_id to check an individual screen. Enter a reason in planned_omission for readings you intended to omit and leave it blank for the rest. The report distinguishes missing readings, unscheduled recordings, and readings with raw gaze alone. Review affected readings shows all the rows behind a finding, one reading at a time, while your trial filters stay in place.

Excel imports use the first worksheet and show its name. ID columns preserve literal labels such as 01 and NA. Leave a cell empty for a missing ID. On restoring a pilot setup, the wizard names files whose headers or time units differ from the saved mapping.

Under Name → Dataset citation, an upload can carry its title, authors or lab, version, DOI, and preferred credit. An unpublished study can supply just its preferred wording. Reopen Edit dataset to revise the credit. Cite and the export bundle include these references alongside the software citation.

docs.title: Scanpath visualization
docs.text:
1. Views and Help.
  2. The Essentials | Full switch (below).
  3. The trial control bar: dataset, trial, screen, sort (⇅) and filter ().
  4. The trial's summary.
  5. The figure.
  6. Plot controls.
  7. The tabs: Annotations, Stimulus & context, Comparisons, Export and Share.

The Scanpath View draws one reading at a time, at the size of the screen it was recorded on.

Looking for a specific button?

All controls lists every button and setting on this view, menu by menu, with a picture of each menu. Search it for what you want to change, such as saccade color or legend position.

docs.title: Essentials and Full
docs.text:
The Scanpath View opens in Essentials, with the main controls for exploring a reading. Switch to Full in the top bar whenever you want more options. The app remembers your choice in this browser.

Essentials shows:

  • the dataset and trial pickers with ◀ ▶;
  • the plot, which starts with a replay on a new visit;
  • the Animation tile, five static views and the Palette tiles;
  • the Export tab, for the figure on screen, and Share.

The More buttons show which additional controls are available in Full and offer Switch to Full. Both modes keep the selected view and palette. An active comparison keeps its switch in Essentials. Settings you chose in Full, such as trial filters, remain active in Essentials; a short note tells you when they apply. Starting a tutorial from Help switches to Full for the current visit. Corpus Analysis and Data Management are the same in both modes.

To open a mode for one visit, add ?ui=full or ?ui=essentials to the app's address (use & if the address already has a ?). This leaves your saved choice unchanged. Links created with Share use the recipient's own mode.

The numbered regions above and the rest of this guide describe Full.

docs.title: Choose a trial
docs.text:
Pick a trial in Select trial above the plot, or step through the list with ◀ ▶. The filter () beside it narrows the list by text, participant, condition or annotation, and ⇅ sorts it. On a trial recorded over several screens, Screen picks the screen to draw. When several participants have the same trial ID, the list shows each reading with its participant in brackets, such as 3 [p2].

All controls → Trial control bar describes each control.

docs.title: Keyboard shortcuts
docs.text:
With focus on Keys Action The page, plot background or trial arrow buttons Left / Right Previous or next trial in the current list (A in Compare) The page, plot background or trial arrow buttons Shift+Left / Shift+Right Previous or next trial for B in Compare The page or plot background Space Play or pause the replay The Replay time slider Left / Right Pause and step one frame The Replay time slider Home / End Jump to the first or last frame The Replay time slider Space Play or pause from the current frame

With A and B together on, either pair of trial shortcuts steps both readings. Use Tab and Shift+Tab to reach the replay controls. The slider keys also work in downloaded HTML replays.

docs.title: Control the layers
docs.text:
Both modes start with the same Presets tiles and Palette. In Full, use Find a setting to jump to a control by name, or open Layers to change what appears in the plot. Click a layer’s name to edit its settings or its switch to show or hide it. Choose Axes to chart the reading by fixation order or time. Figure holds the settings for the whole plot, including framing, titles and legends.

Gaze over time plots elapsed seconds along the horizontal axis and horizontal screen position in pixels on the vertical axis. The length of each horizontal bar shows how long the fixation lasted. Turn Animation on to replay the reading on the text, then off to return to the same chart. Custom brings back your last hand-edited figure.

Section What it controls Presets switch Animation on or off, or choose Scanpath, Heatmap, Illustration, Gaze over time or Custom My presets save a named preset, apply it to another reading, or share it Palette choose Colorblind-safe, Grayscale, or High contrast Compare readings add a second reading over this one, beside it, or below it Playback settings set playback speed, autoplay, and frame quality Fixations the fixation markers: color, shape and size, and the fixation index Saccades the saccade lines and arrows, in one color, by direction or by saccade type Stimulus the text (or redacted blocks), highlighted words, the stimulus image, the font and the background Word boxes each word's box: outline and fill, color and opacity Heatmap where fixations concentrate, by fixation count or duration Raw gaze the gaze samples as recorded Filters & highlights which fixations and saccades are drawn, and which stand out Axes chart presets, X and Y fields, and the coordinate grid Figure screen framing, title and labels, hover fields and legends

All controls → Plot controls describes every setting in each menu.

docs.title: Under the plot
docs.text:
Tab What it is for Annotations Star, tag and write notes on the trial, to find or filter it later. Stimulus & context The trial's context, such as its title, question and answers, and its highlighted word spans. Comparisons Show the other trials that share a field with this one, such as other readings of the same text, in a grid of small figures. Export Download the figure on screen (PNG, SVG, PDF or HTML) or its replay (HTML, GIF or MP4), or build a zip bundle of figures and data for many trials. Share Link reopens this trial with these settings for anyone who has the same dataset. Code gives the Python or CLI code that redraws the figure. Settings file saves the plot settings and restores them.

All controls → Under the plot lists each tab's controls.

Watch the tabs under the figure

docs.title: Render in code
docs.text:
Set up a figure in the app, then open Share → Code for the Python or CLI code that redraws it. For a dataset you imported, replace the placeholder file paths with your own.

Python and CLI: render the demo PythonCLI 
import scanpath_studio as sps

words, fixations = sps.load_sample_data()
fig = sps.plot_scanpath(
    words, fixations, "l37_273", "l37_273_2_1_1_Ele", screen="Paragraph"
)
sps.save_figure(fig, "scanpath.html")

scanpath-studio render --sample \
  -p l37_273 -t l37_273_2_1_1_Ele --screen Paragraph -o scanpath.html

For your own files, use the data loaders. The figure options table lists every figure setting with its Python keyword and CLI flag. For more CLI examples, see Common tasks.

The gallery shows how to make heatmaps, comparisons, replays and other figures in the app, the CLI and Python. For batch export and GIF or MP4 replays, see Export and share.

docs.title: Back up your work
docs.text:
You can save each of these to a file and load it again:

What Where figure settings Share → Settings file favorites, tags and notes Data Management → Current dataset → Annotations → Export column mapping and recording setup Edit dataset → Download setup file saved figure designs My presets → Export

Keep your source data alongside these files, and load the same dataset before restoring them. In the desktop app or a local install, the app also keeps your datasets, annotations and designs between sessions. See Data Management → Saved work → Your session.

docs.title: All controls
docs.text:
Find every control in the Scanpath View, in the order it appears on screen. Search this page (Ctrl+F, or Cmd+F on a Mac) for what you want to change, such as colors, legends or axes.

The view has two sets of controls:

  • The trial control bar, above the plot, decides what you see: the dataset, the trial, and which trials are in the list.
  • The plot controls, the column on the right, decide how it is drawn: each layer of the figure, its colors and sizes, and the figure as a whole.

Use the tabs under the plot to annotate the current trial, read its context, compare readings, export a figure or share the view. For how the parts fit together, see the Scanpath visualization guide.

For the corresponding Python keywords and CLI flags, use the figure options table.

docs.title: Trial control bar
docs.text:
The bar above the plot: pick a dataset and a trial, step through the trials, and narrow, sort or label the list. Essentials has all of it except the slider, ⇅, the filter () and the trial summary table with its pencil (), which are in Full.

Control What it does Select dataset The dataset the view shows. → Draw a scanpath Write a text and place its fixations by hand, as a new dataset. → Import files Upload your own Fixations and Words tables as a new dataset. Select trial The trial to show. Click it and type to narrow the list. Slider Move through the trials in the list. ◀ ▶ The previous or next trial. You can also use Left and Right from the page or plot background. ⇅ → Sort trials by Reorder the trial list by a statistic (such as reading time), a participant, text or condition field, or a column of a metadata table you attached. ⇅ → Descending Reverse that order. → Text / Participant Keep only these texts or participants. Empty keeps all. → a field of your data Keep only trials with these values, or, for a number, in this range. → By participant / By trial / By text The same, for the columns of an attached metadata table. → Favorites only Keep only starred trials. → With any of these tags Keep only trials with any of these tags. → Excluding tags Hide trials with any of these tags, such as To exclude. → ✕ Clear all filters Reset every filter in the panel. Filtered: line under the trial picker Shown while any filter is on, with a dot on : how many of the dataset's trials the filters keep, which filters they are, and ✕ Clear filters to reset them all. → Show the trial summary above the plot Show or hide the row of facts about the trial above the plot. → field lists Drag fields between Shown and Available to choose the trial summary's fields, and drag within Shown to reorder them. Available holds every field with one value per trial: participant, text and condition columns, the columns of any metadata table you attached, and statistics such as reading time and fixation count. → Field colors Give a field a highlight color. Its ✕ puts it back to the default gray. → Refresh fields Check again which fields have one value per trial. Screen and its ◀ ▶ On a trial recorded over several screens: the screen to show.

docs.title: Plot controls
docs.text:
The column has four parts: Presets, Palette, Modes and Customize. The Presets and Palette tiles appear in both modes, and in Full, My presets sits below the preset tiles. Click beside any of the four labels to fold that part away, and the browser remembers it for your next visit. A folded Presets, Palette or Modes line still names the current choice. Under Modes, the switches turn on comparison and, in Full, Playback, and the arrow beside each switch opens its settings. Beside a tall figure, the column scrolls on its own.

  • Layers lists what the plot can draw. Click a layer’s name to edit its settings. The switch on the right shows or hides it. Filters & highlights applies to the current reading.
  • Axes chooses the X and Y fields and configures the coordinate grid.
  • Figure holds framing, titles, hover fields and legends.

Use Find a setting in Full when you know what you want to change. Type a word such as arrow, font or margin and choose a result to open its controls. You can also browse Layers, Axes and Figure. Each menu shows the common adjustments first. Open a named section for finer changes.

If you switch to Essentials while comparing readings, the comparison switch stays available.

docs.title: Playback settings
docs.text:
Turn on the Animation tile, or the Playback switch under Modes, to replay the reading. Use the play and pause buttons and the time slider above the plot. Switch Animation off to return to your figure. For a saccades-only replay, open Full, leave Saccades on, and turn Fixations off. Each line appears when the reading reaches its next fixation. Heatmap and Raw gaze are available in static views. For playback and frame stepping from the keyboard, see Keyboard shortcuts. Open Playback settings in Full for these controls:

Control What it does Speed How fast the video plays, from ×0.25 to ×8: ×1 is the participant's recorded pace, ×2 twice as fast, ×0.5 half as fast. Autoplay Start playing the animation as soon as the plot is shown. Otherwise it starts when you click play. Duration For information only: the trial's reading time, and how long the video runs at this speed. Smoothness How smooth the video is: Coarse, Standard or Fine. More frames play more smoothly but take longer to build. Moving either slider below makes it Custom. Frame timing → Frame interval Reading time between frames, in ms. Frame timing → Frame limit The maximum number of frames in the replay. For long trials, frames are spaced farther apart to stay within this limit. Frame count Shows the number of frames in this replay and the reading time between them.

docs.title: Compare
docs.text:
Compare readings shows a second scanpath, B, beside or over this one. To find everyone who read the same text, open the Comparisons tab and match on text. Pick B in the trial control bar, above the plot. Its ▾ holds:

Control What it does Layout Overlay both scanpaths, or give each a panel, Side by side or Top & bottom. In Animation, the comparison is an overlay. Overlay text In an overlay, whose word boxes and text are drawn: Both, A or B. Reading labels → Label A / Label B Each reading’s name in the comparison legend and above its panel in a split view, written with fields such as {participant_id}. Empty uses the automatic label. Reading labels → Available fields The fields a label can use. Trial arrows ◀ ▶ move both scanpaths at once.

docs.title: Presets, palette and saved presets
docs.text:
Restyle the whole figure in one click, with a ready-made preset or one you saved:

Control What it does Scanpath / Heatmap / Illustration Ready-made presets: fixations and saccades over the text, a word-box heatmap, or a clean schematic. Gaze over time Plot horizontal fixation position (pixels) against time (seconds since the first fixation onset). Each bar spans one fixation. Each displayed reading needs recorded fixation onsets. Compare shows the two readings in separate panels, with time starting at each reading’s first fixation. Custom Restore your last hand-edited figure, including its axes and palette. On first use, start with the figure on screen. My presets Your saved presets. Click one to apply it. renames it and deletes it. My presets → Save the settings on screen as a named preset, to apply again later in one click. My presets → Export / Import Download your presets as a file, or load a file of presets, to share a look with co-authors or move your presets to another computer. A preset in the file replaces yours of the same name. Palette Choose Colorblind-safe, Grayscale for print, or High contrast. The swatches preview each palette’s colors. For a grayscale comparison, A has filled markers and solid lines, and B has hollow markers and dashed lines.

docs.title: Fixations
docs.text:
Click Fixations to edit the markers. The switch shows or hides them.

Control What it does Color One color paints all fixations alike. A number such as duration uses a continuous scale. A category, such as a condition or a part of speech, keeps the same color in every trial of the dataset, even when filtering removes other categories. Up to 20 categories in the dataset get clearly different colors; with more, some colors are closer. The legend identifies missing values separately. color box With One color: the fixation marker color. With a number column: the color scale. Color range and color bar → Range When markers are colored by a number: the values at the two ends of the color scale. Auto fits each trial. Marker appearance → Shape Choose the fixation marker shape: circle, square, diamond, triangle, cross, X, star, hexagon or heart. Size Set the marker size range: the smallest and largest marker diameter, in px. Size by duration → Scale Choose how duration sets marker size: square root (the default), linear, log, or relative to this figure (its shortest to its longest fixation). Size by duration → Durations Set the durations (ms) that get the smallest and the largest marker. Not used on the relative scale. Opacity Set the fixation marker opacity. Lower it to see overlapping fixations. Marker appearance → Outline Set the width (px) and color of the ring around each marker. A width of 0 draws none. Color range and color bar → Show Show the color scale's bar, when markers are colored by a number. Color range and color bar → Vertical / Horizontal, Angle, Size, Thickness, Length Set the bar's direction (right of the plot or below it), its tick-label angle and size, and its thickness and length. Fixation index → Show Number each fixation in reading order. Fixation index → color, Size Choose the numbers' size in every view. For one scanpath, choose their color here. When comparing two scanpaths, each number uses its scanpath’s fixation color, including during replay. Marker appearance → Number position Put each number above its fixation, inside it, or below it. Position on the text → Snap to line Move each fixation up or down onto its line of text. Choose Show positions before snapping above the figure to see the original trial coordinates beside the illustration, on the same axes. Downloads use the illustration. Position on the text → Position Choose where on its line a snapped fixation sits.

docs.title: Saccades
docs.text:
Click Saccades to edit the lines between fixations. The switch shows or hides the lines.

Control What it does Color Choose what decides the saccade color: One color for all; Forward / regression, two colors; or By type, a color per saccade type (forward, skip, refixation, return sweep, regression), with a legend. Forward / regression and By type need a word ID for each fixation, the word it landed on, mapped as the Fixations table's Word ID (such as EyeLink's CURRENT_FIX_INTEREST_AREA_ID). Without one, every saccade is drawn as Off the text. color box With One color: the saccade line color. Types With Forward / regression or By type: the color of each group, such as regressions or return sweeps. Line and arrow appearance → Style Choose the saccade line style: solid, dashed, dotted or dash-dot. Width Set the saccade line width (thickness), in px. Line and arrow appearance → Opacity Set the saccade line and arrow opacity. Lower it to bring the fixations forward. Line and arrow appearance → Shape Choose the saccade shape. Straight draws lines. Arc draws arcs over the text, a schematic labeled Illustration. Direction arrows → Show Show saccade direction arrows: an arrowhead on each saccade, pointing where the eye went. Line and arrow appearance → Arrow size Set the saccade arrowhead size.

docs.title: Stimulus
docs.text:
The Stimulus switch draws the text and the stimulus image. The text rows start from the dataset's Recording setup. Click Stimulus to adjust the text or image for this figure.

Control What it does Text → Show Show the stimulus text, the words the participant read, at their place on the screen. Text → Redact Mask stimulus words and their text IDs. Other columns selected under Figure → Hover fields still travel with the HTML figure. Review those selections and the separate Stimulus image switch before sharing. Text appearance → Fit → Fit to word boxes Size the stimulus text from its word boxes, instead of a fixed font size. Text appearance → Fit → Spacing With Fit to word boxes on: the distance between lines, in font sizes. The font size is that distance divided by this value, so 3 leaves a blank line above and below. Text appearance → Size With Fit to word boxes on: the size of the axis and legend text, in px. Off: the stimulus text's size too, in px or pt. Text appearance → Font Choose the stimulus text font (typeface). Other font… takes any font name. Text appearance → Color → text color Choose the stimulus text color. Word highlights → Show Highlight words in the stimulus text, such as the answer span. Word highlights → word column Choose which words to highlight: a true/false word column, such as the critical span. Word highlights → Style Mark text changes the color of the selected words. Mark border outlines the span. Both have a color picker. Underline draws a line beneath each selected word in the current text color. A border can stay visible with text and ordinary word boxes hidden. Each split panel outlines its own stimulus. Stimulus image → Show Show the stimulus image, the screen as shown in the experiment, under the scanpath. Stimulus image → File Upload a stimulus image (PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP) to draw under the scanpath. It replaces the dataset's image and is not included in Share links. Stimulus image → Opacity Set the stimulus image opacity. Lower it so the scanpath reads over it. Stimulus image → Offset → X / Y Move (nudge) the stimulus image left, right, up or down, in px, to line it up with the word boxes. Stimulus image → Scale Resize (scale) the stimulus image so its text matches the word boxes.

docs.title: Word boxes
docs.text:
The Word boxes switch draws each word’s interest area. Click Word boxes to set its outline and fill.

Control What it does Outline color Choose the word box outline (border) color. Outline opacity Set the word box outline opacity. 0 hides the outlines. Fill color Choose the word box fill color, inside each box. Fill opacity Set the word box fill opacity. 0 draws outlines only.

docs.title: Heatmap
docs.text:
The Heatmap switch shows where reading concentrated. Click Heatmap to choose the measure, colors and scale.

Control What it does Draw as Choose the heatmap style: Word boxes colors each word box, Smoothed blurs the fixations with a Gaussian. Compare always uses word boxes. Smoothing and scale → Blur For Smoothed: how far each fixation spreads, in px. Auto picks it from the size of the data. Measure Choose what the heatmap measures: total fixation duration (dwell time), or Fixation count. Colors Choose the heatmap colors (color scale). Smoothing and scale → Scale Choose a linear or log heatmap scale. Smoothing and scale → Range A word-box legend gives the reading’s dwell-time or count limits. Choose Use this heatmap range for other trials above the plot to keep those limits. Smoothed heatmaps scale to each figure’s peak. Opacity Set the heatmap opacity. Auto uses 0.5 for word boxes and 0.45 for smoothed. Color bar → Show, orientation, Angle, Size, Thickness, Length Show the heatmap color bar, and set its orientation, label angle and size, thickness and length.

docs.title: Raw gaze
docs.text:
The Raw gaze switch draws the recorded gaze samples. Click Raw gaze to set their appearance.

Control What it does Sample color A single reading uses sample time, or sample order when timestamps are missing. Choose the fallback color here. In Compare, each reading has its own color. Dot size Set the raw gaze sample marker size. Opacity Set the raw gaze sample opacity.

To inspect samples from one reading, open Axes → Axis layout. Choose Horizontal gaze position over recorded time, Vertical gaze position over recorded time, or a recorded pupil measurement. These presets turn on Raw gaze. A recording without timestamps offers sample number on the horizontal axis.

In the OneStop demo, the clock starts at trial onset and each screen's samples start when the reader sees that screen. A sample with missing gaze coordinates has no pupil area either, so the pupil chart shows a gap there. The raw table and its exports keep those samples.

docs.title: Filters & highlights
docs.text:
An Active label appears beside Filters & highlights when either reading has a fixation window, highlight or filter in effect. The trial-list filter selects whole readings.

Control What it does Fixations → Index range Show only some fixations: a range of the reading order, such as fixations 10 to 40. Keep this range across trials Keep that fixation range when you move to another trial. Off, it applies to this trial only, and the next trial shows all its fixations. Short / Long Find fixations shorter or longer than the cutoff (80 ms and 800 ms by default). Show keeps the usual marker and Highlight changes its appearance. Hide removes the marker and skips the fixation in replay and fixation-index sequences. Replay lines connect the remaining fixations. Spatial saccade lines and heatmaps on static plots still use the hidden fixation. Outside the text Highlight or hide fixations that land in no word box. Near a blink Highlight or hide fixations at or next to a blink (needs a blink column). Highlight markers → shape and color Choose the marker shape and color of each highlighted fixation kind. Saccades → Types Show only some saccade types, such as regressions or return sweeps. Empty draws all. Needs a word ID for each fixation, as for coloring saccades by type.

docs.title: Axes
docs.text:
Choose a chart preset, or set the X and Y fields individually. Open Coordinate grid to style the screen grid.

Control What it does Axis layout Plot horizontal or vertical screen position by fixation index or elapsed time, compare fixation index with elapsed time or duration, or plot fixation index by the word each fixation landed on. Reverse horizontal axis and Reverse vertical axis run a chart axis the other way, for example to put the first fixation at the top; the screen view keeps the stimulus as shown. Connect fixations traces the windowed index sequence, including with fixation markers hidden. Hide filters also apply to the line. On an elapsed-time chart, each bar spans one fixation’s duration. Zero is the trial’s first recorded onset, including when viewing a later screen or a narrower fixation window. Choose axis fields → horizontal / vertical Choose fixation fields or raw gaze measurements. For samples, try pupil size or gaze position against recorded time or sample number. Each layer draws the fields it contains. Screen Y increases downward. Screen X and Y restores the stimulus view. Static comparisons use shared ranges in side-by-side or stacked panels. Each reading keeps its own elapsed-time origin. Animation uses screen coordinates. Grid → Show Show a grid of screen coordinates, in px. Grid spacing and labels → interval Set the grid spacing (interval), in px, or let Auto choose it. Grid spacing and labels → label size Set the grid label (tick label) font size.

Each dot is a fixation. The clusters step down as the reader looks lower on the screen. Around 39 seconds, the reader looks back near the top.

docs.title: Figure
docs.text:
Open Screen & framing, Title & labels, Hover fields, or Legends.

Control What it does Screen & framing → Background Choose the figure background color. Crop to data Crop (zoom) the figure to the part of the screen with data, instead of the whole screen. Margins and border color → crop margin Set the crop margin: the space around the data when cropping. Auto uses 5% of the data's width and height, at least 20 px. Show plot border, Margins and border color Show a 1 px border around the plot area, and choose its color. It marks the edge of the screen, or, with Crop to data, the edge of the cropped area. Illustration label → When to show the label Choose when the figure carries an Illustration note, saying it does not show the recorded positions. Auto adds it when a setting changes the geometry or the data (such as snapping fixations to a line or drawing saccades as arcs), Show always, Hide never. Illustration label → Label text Write the Illustration label's text. Empty writes "Illustration ·" followed by the reasons. Show title, title text and Text size and color Add a figure title above the plot, and set its font size. {field} inserts a value of the trial. Show caption, caption text and Text size and color Add a figure caption below the plot, and set its font size and color. {field} works here too. Credit → Show Add a small Made with Scanpath Studio line under the plot. Hover fields → Fields on a word / Fields on a fixation Choose the hover fields: what the tooltip shows when the mouse is over a word or a fixation. Legends → Show on the figure Show or hide each legend the figure draws: Compare (A/B), Saccade types, Fixation colors, Fixation sizes or Text highlight. The fixation size legend starts hidden. Select Fixation sizes to include it in a saved figure. Legend position and style → Position Choose the legend position: a corner, the middle of an edge, or down a side, outside or inside the plot. Legend position and style → Arrangement Choose the legend arrangement: Stacked or Side by side. Legend position and style → Text size Set the legend text (font) size, in px. Empty uses the figure's text size.

docs.title: Reset
docs.text:
At the foot of Full plot controls, use the arrows beside Reset to step through your last 30 plot changes. Presets and a confirmed reset each count as one change.

Control What it does Undo Restore the previous plot settings for the current dataset. Switching trials keeps you on the newly selected trial. Redo Reapply the change you undid. Making a new plot edit clears the redo list. Reset After you confirm, reset every plot setting to its default, Filters & highlights included. Annotations, trial filters, data and the selected trial stay.

Changing datasets starts a fresh history. A trial-specific fixation window drops out of history when you leave that reading.

docs.title: In Compare
docs.text:
With Compare on, scanpath B gets a second row in the trial control bar, and several menus split into a Scanpath A and a Scanpath B group.

Control What it does Dataset B Choose the dataset scanpath B comes from. To reopen a shared comparison with PoTeC or OneStop, the recipient needs the corpus on their computer. If the link opens only A, open the named corpus as the main dataset to locate or download its files, then reopen the link. Trial B, slider, ◀ ▶ Choose scanpath B's trial: 📄 marks the same text, 👤 the same participant. Screen B On a trial recorded over several screens: B's screen to show. ⇅ on B's row Sort scanpath B's trial list, apart from A's. The default, Same text, then same participant, lists trials of A's text first, then A's participant, then the rest. You can also sort by any field, as on A's row. on B's row Filter scanpath B's trials, apart from A's. Layers → Fixations → Scanpath A / B → Color, Size, Opacity Choose each scanpath's fixation marker color, size range and opacity. When the markers are colored by a column, Color becomes Outline. Layers → Saccades → Scanpath A / B → Color, Style, Width Choose each scanpath's saccade line color, style and width. Layers → Word boxes → Scanpath A / B → Line, Fill Choose each scanpath's word box outline and fill colors and opacities. Layers → Heatmap → Scanpath A / B → Colors Choose each scanpath's heatmap colors (color scale). Layers → Raw gaze → Scanpath A / B → Color Choose each scanpath's raw gaze sample color. Layers → Filters & highlights → Reading B Set scanpath B's fixation range, fixation highlights and saccade types.

docs.title: Under the plot
docs.text:
The tabs under the figure. Essentials has Export, for the current figure, and Share; the other tabs and the export bundle are in Full.

Tab Control What it does Annotations Favorite Star the trial as a favorite, to find it again with Favorites only in the trial filters. Tags / Add a tag Tag the trial, with an existing tag or a new one, such as exclude. Tags let you filter the trial list later: the in the trial control bar keeps or hides trials by tag. Notes Write a free-text note on the trial. Stimulus & context Fields → Context fields Choose the trial context to show, such as the text's title, a question or an answer. Fields → Highlighted spans Choose true/false word columns to highlight in the text, each with a summary line. Comparisons Match field Compare with other trials: show the trials that share this trial's value of a field, such as the same text. Columns Set how many comparison panels per row, from 1 to 4. Export Download format Export (download) the figure on screen as PNG, SVG, PDF or HTML, or the animation as an HTML, GIF or MP4 video. Width, unit, DPI Set the PNG export size for print: width (mm or in) and resolution (DPI). A blank width writes the figure at three times its screen size. Trials to include Choose which trials to export in the bundle: This trial, All filtered trials, All trials of one participant, All trials of one text, or All trials, ignoring filters. Formats / Tabular data / Table format Choose the bundle's figure formats, the data tables to include, and their format (CSV, Parquet or both). Layers as separate files Export each visual layer (fixations, saccades, word boxes…) as a separate file, to stack in a vector editor. Annotations (JSON) / Settings file (JSON) Settings file: beside each trial's figure, a plot_config.json recording how it was drawn (layers, colors, sizes, screen, title and caption), so the figures are documented. Annotations: one annotations.json with the exported trials' favorites, tags and notes, which Data Management → Current dataset → Annotations can import again. File path pattern Set the file names inside the export bundle. Build export Build the export bundle (a zip) to download. Share Link Copy a link that reopens this trial and its settings. The bundled demo works anywhere. A public dataset has to be downloaded on the recipient's side. For each dataset you imported, send its data files and setup file (Current dataset → Edit dataset → Download setup file) so they can add it under the same name. If they have A but still need B for a comparison, the link opens A and names the dataset to add. On your own computer the link still works after either dataset is renamed. A localhost link opens where the app runs at the same address. Code → Python / CLI, Show every option Get the Python or command-line code that redraws this figure, for scripts and reproduction. Settings file → Download settings / Restore settings Save the plot settings to a file, or load (restore) a saved settings file.

docs.text:
Choose a task below. If you're new to the app, start with Get started. The feature guides explain the controls in more detail.

  • Optimize data collection

    • Review an experimenter's sessions

  • Filter data

    • Exclude unsuitable trials
    • Select participants by a field

  • Export customized figures

  • Analyze a corpus

docs.title: Analyze a corpus
docs.text:
• Analyze one text

    Compare word-by-word measures across participants.

  • Compare groups or conditions

    Inspect group means and differences.

  • Track changes over time

    Inspect trends within or across trials.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text:
Open a dataset and set the trial filters for your question. Word-level views need reading measures in the Words table; the bundled demo includes them. To compare participants on one text, their trials of that text must share one text ID.

Choose Texts to compare passages or Participants to compare readers. Select a dot to see its mean, range and how many readings contributed. Open word profile shows where in a text the values change. Open participant profile compares one reader’s word values with the others.

docs.title: Keep the result
docs.text:
Open Table and downloads under a text or participant comparison. In a detailed analysis that produces a table, use Download results. The CSV saves the values. Download recipe (JSON) saves the dataset name, the trial filters, the analysis choices and the counts. Keep the source data alongside the recipe so you can reproduce the result.

To draw a summary with Python or the CLI, see Plot a summary in code.

docs.title: Analyze one text
docs.text:
1. Select the trials, then open Corpus Analysis and choose a Reading measure. In the bundled demo, try Total fixation duration — TFD.
  2. In Texts, select a dot or use Find a text, then choose Open word profile. The Cohort profile shows a point for each word with enough observations. Hover over a point to read the word and its value.
  3. Open Readings behind a word to check which participants supplied a value. A blank cell means that reading had no recorded value for the selected measure. In Chart settings, Aggregate sets how the profile combines values, Spread controls the shaded band, and Min participants per word sets how many readers must contribute.
  4. In Chart settings, use View to explore the same text. Measure on the stimulus colors the words in their original positions. Measure vs feature compares the reading measure with a feature in the Words table, such as surprisal.
  5. Download the table and recipe.

If your data has no mapped Text ID, open Texts to inspect a single reading by its trial ID. To compare several readings, map the Words column that identifies the same passage across participants. If the page asks for reading measures, Map reading measures opens the column mapping for an editable dataset. For an upload that contains only fixations or gaze samples, Add a Words table opens the editor where you can attach the report.

The recording shows total fixation duration on a text, against GPT-2 surprisal, and between two groups.

docs.title: Compare groups or conditions
docs.text:
To compare two reading conditions in the bundled demo, use the advanced (Adv) and elementary (Ele) versions of its texts.

  1. Select the trials, then open Corpus Analysis and select Groups. Choose a measure.
  2. In Edit groups, use Split a field and choose difficulty_level. Select Adv for Group A and Ele for Group B. Each group needs at least one value. To choose participants, texts or conditions separately for each group, use Independent filter sets. A group with no filters includes all selected trials.
  3. Read Difference (A − B). For total fixation duration, a difference of 20 ms means that Group A spent 20 ms longer per word on average. The counts show how many participants contributed a value to each mean. For a rate, a change from 30% in B to 40% in A is a difference of 10 percentage points.
  4. Download the table and recipe.

For a different comparison, open Chart settings and choose a View. To explore Group A on its own, turn off Compare two groups.

For each participant, Group means & difference averages the words with a recorded value across all their selected trials. A trial with more measured words has more weight in that participant's mean. The group mean then gives each participant equal weight. In Participants, each reading contributes one mean to the summary, so the two views can give different values.

A participant who read both conditions contributes to both group means. The Standardized difference (Cohen's d) is available only for groups with no participants in common.

docs.title: Track changes over time
docs.text:
Inspect a measure within trials or across a session.

  1. Select the trials and open Corpus Analysis.

  2. To follow one reader, choose Participants, select a reader and open their profile. To follow a group, choose Groups and turn off Compare two groups. In Chart settings, choose the View you need.

    Scope View One participant across trials Per-trial trend Fixation duration within trials, pooled for one participant Fixation duration over time A group across trials Group trend

  3. Choose a measure, and an Aggregate where the view offers one. Across-trial trends order each participant's trials by a trial_index or TRIAL_INDEX column. Without one, the app orders them by fixation time, or as listed, and this may differ from the order the trials were shown. For the within-trial view, set X axis to Fixation order, or to Time (ms) when the data records fixation onsets.

  4. Download the table and recipe.

docs.title: Optimize data collection
docs.text:
• Check a session

    Inspect a pilot or completed recording.

  • Compare two eye trackers

    Review recordings of the same text.

  • Review an experimenter's sessions

    Review sessions by who collected them.

Start with a loaded dataset. To apply exclusion decisions after reviewing, use Filter data.

docs.title: Review an experimenter's sessions
docs.text:
Review recordings collected by one experimenter.

Before you start, switch to Full at the top of the Scanpath View (Essentials and Full).

  1. Keep the experimenter column when you import the data, under Extra fields to keep. If each participant had one experimenter, you can instead attach it in a participant metadata table.
  2. Open the filter () beside Select trial and choose the experimenter. Columns of a participant metadata table are under By participant.
  3. Inspect and replay their trials.
  4. In Annotations, tag trials review and note recurring problems.
  5. Export the review.

To compare experimenters, turn on Compare. Use the filter on each scanpath's row to pick a different experimenter, and choose readings of the same text.

docs.title: Check a session
docs.text:
Inspect a recording and save the trials that need attention.

Before you start, switch to Full at the top of the Scanpath View (Essentials and Full).

docs.title: 1. Open the session
docs.text: Import your tables, or select a loaded dataset. Check that its Recording setup matches the screen used in the experiment.

docs.title: 2. Inspect a trial
docs.text:
In the Scanpath View, pick a trial in Select trial. Turn on Word boxes and check:

  • whether the boxes match the stimulus image, if you have one;
  • where the fixations sit relative to the words;
  • unexpected gaps, shifts or off-screen positions.

For a consistent offset, check coordinate units and screen setup.

docs.title: 3. Replay the recording
docs.text: Choose Animation to follow the fixation order and timing. To mark short or long fixations, or fixations outside the text, open Filters & highlights ▾ → Fixations and set Short, Long or Outside the text to Highlight. A gap or an unusual scanpath does not tell you its cause.

docs.title: 4. Record the review
docs.text: In Annotations, tag the trial review and write what you observed in Notes. Use ◀ ▶ beside Select trial to move through the session.

docs.title: 5. Save the review
docs.text:
Export favorites, tags and notes from Data Management → Current dataset → Annotations → Export. The file includes participant and trial IDs. Open on an annotation row returns to that trial.

To reconcile a second reviewer's notes, choose Import. The preview counts new, identical and differing entries. Open disputed reading displays both entries beside the scanpath for that reading. You can download the differences for discussion. Apply import adds new entries and keeps the current version of a differing note unless you select the replacement option.

For exclusion decisions, follow Exclude unsuitable trials.

docs.title: Compare two eye trackers
docs.text:
Review the same text recorded with two trackers or setups.

Before you start, switch to Full at the top of the Scanpath View (Essentials and Full).

  1. Import each recording as a separate dataset, each with the Recording setup of its tracker.
  2. Open the first dataset in the Scanpath View and pick a trial.
  3. Turn on Compare. In scanpath B's row, choose the second dataset in Dataset B and a trial of the same text in Trial B.
  4. Compare fixation placement, spread and missing stretches. An overlay needs both datasets recorded on the same screen size. Otherwise the app shows the two scanpaths side by side.

This recording compares two participants in the bundled demo. For two trackers, choose the second recording in Dataset B.

Use the session-review steps to save observations.

docs.title: Filter data
docs.text:
• Exclude unsuitable trials

    Leave tagged trials out.

  • Select participants by a field

    Use participant metadata.

  • Find trials with specific fixation patterns

    Select trials after inspecting fixations.

docs.title: Before you start
docs.text: Open a dataset in the Scanpath View. The filter () beside Select trial selects whole trials. Filters & highlights in the Plot controls changes which fixations and saccades the figure draws. Switch to Full at the top of the Scanpath View to use trial filters, fixation highlights, and batch export (Essentials and Full).

docs.title: Check and export the selection
docs.text:
1. Check the remaining trial and participant counts and inspect a few trials.
  2. Follow Export every trial and choose All filtered trials. The bundle's index.csv lists its files with their participant and trial IDs.
  3. Keep a full decision record with Data Management → Annotations → Export. The annotations in a bundle cover only the exported trials.

docs.title: Exclude unsuitable trials
docs.text:
Apply your exclusion criteria and leave rejected trials out of the selection.

Before you start, switch to Full at the top of the Scanpath View (Essentials and Full).

  1. Review the session. Judge each trial against your study's criteria. A scanpath pattern alone does not establish skimming or poor calibration.
  2. In Annotations, tag rejected trials exclude and write a short reason in Notes.
  3. Open the filter () beside Select trial. Under By trial annotation, add exclude to Excluding tags.
  4. Check and export the selection.

For a trial with several screens, tag the whole trial. A tag on one screen does not exclude the trial.

The recording shows favorites and tags. For the selection above, use the exclude tag and Excluding tags.

docs.title: Find trials with specific fixation patterns
docs.text:
Locate trials containing particular fixation patterns.

Before you start, switch to Full at the top of the Scanpath View (Essentials and Full).

  1. Open Filters & highlights ▾ → Fixations.

  2. Set the Mode of the category you need to Highlight:

    • Short or Long, with a duration threshold in ms
    • Outside the text, for fixations in no word box
    • Near a blink, if your data has a blink column

  3. Step through the trials. In Annotations, tag those that meet your analysis criteria, for example include.

  4. Open the filter () beside Select trial. Under By trial annotation, add include to With any of these tags.
  5. Check and export the selection.

docs.title: Select participants by a field
docs.text:
Select participants using metadata such as native language, age or group.

Before you start, switch to Full at the top of the Scanpath View (Essentials and Full).

  1. Attach a participant metadata table, with one row per participant and a participant ID column. When you add a dataset, use Metadata → Participants. For a loaded dataset, use Data Management → Edit dataset → Data tables & column mapping.
  2. Open the filter () beside Select trial and find By participant.
  3. Choose a field and the values or range to keep.
  4. Check the remaining participant IDs and export the selection.

To also apply trial-level quality criteria, follow Exclude unsuitable trials.

docs.title: Export customized figures
docs.text:
• Export one figure

    A static image or interactive HTML.

  • Export a replay

    GIF, MP4 or interactive HTML.

  • Export every trial

    A ZIP of figures and data tables.

For installation requirements or a failed export, see the export FAQ.

docs.title: Export a replay
docs.text:
Save an animated reading for a talk or supplement.

Before you start, switch to Full at the top of the Scanpath View (Essentials and Full).

  1. Pick a trial in the Scanpath View and choose Animation.
  2. In Animation settings → Replay, set the Speed. Turn on the layers you want to show.
  3. Open the Export tab. Under Current figure, set Download format to GIF, MP4 or HTML.
  4. Download the replay. GIF and MP4 play at the selected speed. HTML keeps the interactive playback controls.

Exporting a GIF. The rendering wait is shortened in this recording.

For GIF/MP4 export from Python, see Export and share.

docs.title: Export every trial
docs.text:
Build a ZIP of static figures and data tables for a set of trials.

Before you start, switch to Full at the top of the Scanpath View (Essentials and Full).

  1. Set the figure's design once. Each exported trial uses that design, without animation or a comparison partner.
  2. Open the Export tab. Under Export bundle → Trials to include, choose This trial, All filtered trials, All trials of one participant, All trials of one text or All trials, ignoring filters.
  3. Choose the Figure formats and, under Also include, the tables and their Table format. Check the File path pattern. To edit individual layers later, turn on Layers as separate files.
  4. Click Build export, download the bundle, and inspect one exported figure.

For PNGs, turn on Smaller PNG files to reduce file size at the same resolution. This adds encoding time. Images over 16.8 megapixels use the standard encoding to limit memory use. Outside the app, scanpath-studio render --compact-png and save_figure(..., compact_png=True) do the same for one figure and its layers. PNG scale controls resolution separately. A scale of 1 writes one pixel per figure pixel, and the default scale of 2 doubles both dimensions.

Large bundles are kept on temporary disk and download as one ZIP in a new tab. Keep the Export panel open until the download finishes. If your browser cannot stream the ZIP, the download page offers numbered parts and instructions for joining them.

Exporting figures and tables for the bundled demo's trials. The build is sped up in this recording.

Keep each trial's plot_config.json for the design, README.md for the build details and index.csv for the file list and failures. Keep your original data and record its version and the selected trial filters separately.

For a scripted batch, use the Python recipe in Export and share.

docs.title: Export one figure
docs.text:
Save a scanpath, heatmap or comparison at the size you need.

In either mode, use the view tiles to choose a figure. For Compare readings and My views, switch to Full at the top of the Scanpath View (Essentials and Full).

docs.title: 1. Choose the view
docs.text: Pick a trial in the Scanpath View. Choose a View tile, or set the layers in Full. Turn on Compare if the figure needs two readings. Check that text and markers are readable and nothing is clipped.

docs.title: 2. Set the format and size
docs.text:
Open the Export tab and find Current figure. Choose the Download format:

Output Format Image PNG Vector figure SVG or PDF Interactive figure HTML

For a print PNG, set Width and DPI. For HTML that opens offline, tick Self-contained HTML.

docs.title: 3. Download
docs.text:
Click the download button for the chosen format, such as ⬇ Download PNG.

Exporting a PNG at 180 mm and 300 dpi.

docs.title: 4. Reuse the design or share the figure
docs.text:
• My views in the Plot controls saves the look for other trials.
  • Share → Link reopens the trial and its settings. For data you imported, send the source files and tell the recipient the dataset name shown in the link. They can open the link after importing the files under that name. If a comparison uses two imported datasets, send both. Someone who has only A can open its trial and return to the link after adding B. Your own copy of the link still works if you rename either dataset later.
  • Share → Code gives Python or CLI code that redraws the figure.
  • Share → Settings file → Download settings saves the settings, and Restore settings loads them again.
